title: Two Practical and Provably Secure Block Ciphers: BEAR and LION
bitmessage_link: Payload cipher family behind Sphinx-style formats; unaffected by size growth of KEMs.
note: Wide-block ciphers (hash plus stream cipher, 3 or 4 Feistel rounds) from which LIONESS, the SPRP used for Sphinx payloads, derives. Symmetric only: Grover halves key strength, so 256-bit keys keep 128-bit post-quantum security; the post-quantum cost in Sphinx comes entirely from the public-key header.

title: A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search
bitmessage_link: The only generic quantum speedup for Bitmessage-style hash proof-of-work and for key search.
note: Unstructured search in O(sqrt(N)) queries. Against an n-bit hashcash target the expected work falls from 2^n to about 2^(n/2) hash evaluations in the ideal case; it parallelises poorly (k machines give only sqrt(k) speedup).

title: Private Information Retrieval
bitmessage_link: Replaces broadcast-and-trial-decrypt with indexed private retrieval: the recipient fetches only its slots and the server learns nothing about which; works only if the recipient can compute or look up the slot (a rendezvous or mailbox index)
note: Founding paper. A single database must be downloaded in full (n bits) for perfect privacy; with k>=2 replicated non-colluding servers there are sublinear schemes (two servers: about n^(1/3) communication). The baseline cost every later receiver-privacy scheme is measured against: Bitmessage's flood is the trivial single-server solution.

title: Key-Privacy in Public-Key Encryption
bitmessage_link: The property Bitmessage's flooding relies on: ciphertext must not reveal which key it targets.
note: Defines key-privacy (IK-CPA/IK-CCA, i.e. ANO-CPA/ANO-CCA): a ciphertext must not reveal the recipient key. Every post-quantum KEM used for recipient-hiding must be re-proved against this notion.

title: Hashcash - A Denial of Service Counter-Measure
bitmessage_link: The exact mechanism Bitmessage attaches to every object.
note: Partial-hash-collision stamps as a cost-function against email spam and DoS. Adversary: bulk sender who trades CPU for volume; assumes a roughly uniform sender cost model.

title: The Sybil Attack
bitmessage_link: Why per-identity trust fails in an open flooding network and why Bitmessage ties cost to objects (proof of work) instead of identities.
note: Without a logically central identity authority, an entity can present multiple identities and defeat redundancy-based schemes. Adversary: single entity with many pseudonymous identities, limited only by resources.

title: Herbivore: A Scalable and Efficient Protocol for Anonymous Communication
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.
note: Cost model: DC-net cliques of small size; later Dissent papers report Herbivore-class systems usable only up to 40-50 participants. Background.

title: Public Key Encryption with Keyword Search
bitmessage_link: Lets an untrusted server route messages by keyword/recipient tag without reading them, a pre-Bitmessage alternative to trial decryption by every node.
note: PEKS: a sender appends a searchable tag under the recipient's public key; the recipient hands a trapdoor for a keyword to a gateway that can test tags without reading messages. Built from identity-based encryption; each test is one pairing, so server cost is linear in stored tags. The template for outsourced tag matching (FMD, OMR) and for pub/sub keyword filters.

title: Off-the-Record Communication, or, Why Not To Use PGP

note: Introduced OTR: ephemeral DH with rekeying for forward secrecy, MAC key publication for deniability (malleable encryption), authentication without non-repudiation; the ancestor of the Signal ratchet and the deniability goal.

title: Proof-of-Work Proves Not to Work

note: Argues that PoW cannot separate spammers from legitimate senders because spammers use stolen cycles (zombies) while honest users have weak machines; a cost that spammers will pay is too high for ordinary users. Adversary: botnet-equipped spammer with free compute.

title: A Formal Treatment of Onion Routing

title: Private Searching On Streaming Data

note: A server filters a stream of documents against a hidden keyword criterion using public-key (additively homomorphic) encryption and returns a compact encrypted buffer of matches, without learning the criterion or which documents matched; generalises PIR to a streaming setting and to richer queries. Ancestor of OMR: server work is linear in the stream and the output size is bounded by the expected number of matches.

title: The Loopix Anonymity System
bitmessage_link: Message-oriented, asynchronous alternative to Bitmessage flooding: Poisson-delayed layered mixes with loop and drop cover traffic and semi-trusted providers that store mail for offline users.

title: Stadium: A Distributed Metadata-Private Messaging System
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.
note: Cost model: parallel verifiable mixnet with distributed noise generation; supports 4x more users than Vuvuzela using servers that cost about an order of magnitude less; per-user bandwidth under 5x Vuvuzela; 100-server EC2 deployment. title: Enabling Large-Scale IoT-Based Services through Elastic Publish/Subscribe

title: Dandelion: Redesigning the Bitcoin Network for Anonymity
bitmessage_link: Direct answer to flooding exposing the origin: Bitmessage floods an object to all peers at once so the first-hearing node is a strong source estimator; stem/fluff is the standard repair, and Bitmessage later added a Dandelion-style stem.
note: Introduces Dandelion: transactions first travel a randomly chosen path (stem, anonymity phase) and are then diffused (fluff). title: COPSS-lite: Lightweight ICN Based Pub/Sub for IoT Environments
note: Information Centric Networking is a new networking paradigm that treats content as first class entity.

title: Quantum attacks on Bitcoin, and how to protect against them
bitmessage_link: Directly applicable to Bitmessage's hashcash-style double-SHA-512 proof-of-work and its ECDSA keys.

For a superconducting machine (66.7 MHz gates, physical error 5e-4, difficulty 10^12) the effective hash rate is 13.8 GH/s using 4.4 million physical qubits, over 1000x slower than a 14 TH/s ASIC; scaling is about 0.04 s sqrt(D) so Grover does not parallelise like ASICs. title: The Double Ratchet: Security Notions, Proofs, and Modularization for the Signal Protocol
bitmessage_link: Gives the formal target for session security that Bitmessage's static-key encryption does not reach, and the CKA primitive reused in PQ ratchets.
note: Clean definition of secure messaging (forward security, post-compromise security, immediate decryption) and a modular generalised Signal protocol from continuous key agreement, forward-secure AEAD and a PRF-PRNG. Content/session security only.

Abstracted as the exclusive call-centre problem; no efficient computational-assumption solution found. Private answering machine constructed only under a bounded number of friends, accepting that bound as leakage.

bitmessage_link: Theory behind the hybrid wrappers used in post-quantum onion and mix formats.

title: Untagging Tor: A Formal Treatment of Onion Encryption
bitmessage_link: Formalises the integrity (anti-tagging) property that Bitmessage's static-key layering never attempts.

bitmessage_link: Bitmessage avoids contact discovery by publishing everything, but any scheme that routes by address or tag must solve how a user learns the right address or slot without revealing their contacts.

title: Postal Services over Swarm (pss) README
bitmessage_link: Messages routed towards a recipient overlay address with a prefix of chosen length; the neighbourhood, not the whole network, trial-decrypts. Successor to Whisper for Swarm.

title: Dandelion++: Lightweight Cryptocurrency Networking with Formal Anonymity Guarantees
bitmessage_link: Reference design for hiding origin in a flooding network without encryption; the Bitmessage stem phase and most later P2P messengers that borrow it follow this construction.
note: Dandelion++ replaces per-hop line-graph construction with a 4-regular privacy graph, per-epoch routing and fail-safe timers. Adversary: colluding fraction p of nodes that may deviate from the protocol (drop, inject, collude on duplicates), knows the graph and observes first-receipt times; formal near-optimal precision/recall guarantees with a lightweight local rule.

title: KEM Combiners
bitmessage_link: Underpins mixing a post-quantum KEM with ECDH in a static key setup.

title: Zcash Protocol Specification (Sapling and Orchard note encryption and viewing keys)
bitmessage_link: Concrete deployed analogue of the problem: the per-output scan cost and the bandwidth/privacy compromise made by wallets that cannot afford to download and trial-decrypt everything.

title: Optimal Channel Security Against Fine-Grained State Compromise: The Safety of Messaging
bitmessage_link: Provides the upper bound against which static-key and ratchet designs can be compared.
note: Defines the best possible security of a bidirectional channel against repeated fine-grained state compromise and gives a proven-secure construction (with updatable public-key encryption and signatures) that is strictly stronger than the Double Ratchet; showing that the Double Ratchet is not optimal and at what cost optimal security can be had.

title: Using Publish/Subscribe for Short-lived IoT Data
note: The goal is to identify the/those publish/subscribe proto-col(s) that are best suited for loT data and the metric is end-to-end delay and the recommended approach is the solution that yields the lowest delay under the test conditions.

title: Efficient Ratcheting: Almost-Optimal Guarantees for Secure Messaging
bitmessage_link: Quantifies the efficiency of stronger-than-Signal session security, relevant to the per-message bandwidth cost of any flooded network.
note: Almost-optimal security notion for secure messaging that tolerates exposure of secret state and local randomness (forward secrecy, backward secrecy / healing, immediate decryption), with constructions far more efficient than the optimal-security constructions of Jaeger-Stepanovs and Poettering-Rosler (which pay an extreme efficiency loss compared with Signal) while closing most of the gap to Signal's guarantees.

title: An Empirical Analysis of Anonymity in Zcash
bitmessage_link: Empirical limit on public-ledger sender/recipient hiding; analogous to timing correlation of Bitmessage objects at ingress and egress.
note: Measurement of how Zcash's anonymity set is eroded in practice: most value moves through transparent addresses; heuristics link shielded deposits and withdrawals. Shows ledger-level hiding depends on user behaviour and on timing/value correlations at the shield/unshield boundary.

title: Efficient tree-based content-based routing schemes

title: Karaoke: Distributed Private Messaging Immune to Passive Traffic Analysis
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.

Trust: differential privacy with a fraction of servers honest.

title: Cwtch: Privacy Preserving Infrastructure for Asynchronous, Decentralized, Multi-Party and Metadata Resistant Applications
bitmessage_link: Closest analogue to Bitmessage chans: group fetch of all group messages from an untrusted server, but scoped to a small group and routed over Tor, not network-wide.
note: Extends Ricochet with offline delivery and groups via untrusted, discardable Cwtch servers that relay group messages over Tor v3 onion services. Hides: IP of each party (Tor), content (E2EE), contact relationships from servers (servers see only group traffic; every member fetches all group messages). Leaks: group membership is not hidden from servers; all group members download all group messages (flood within group)

title: Lattice-Based Group Signatures: Achieving Full Dynamicity (and Deniability) with Ease
bitmessage_link: Group signature route to anonymous-but-accountable posting, post-quantum.

title: Key-Insulated and Privacy-Preserving Signature Scheme with Publicly Derived Public Key

title: Technology preview: Sealed sender for Signal
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage hides the recipient by flooding; sealed sender hides the sender but exposes the recipient to the server, the opposite split. Delivery tokens are the analogue of Bitmessage's proof-of-work admission.

title: Understanding Tor Usage with Privacy-Preserving Measurement

title: Shared-Dining: Broadcasting Secret Shares using Dining-Cryptographers Groups
bitmessage_link: Enforces anonymity in the DC-then-flood design that forwarders have no incentive to honour.
note: (n,k)-Shamir sharing of the message inside a DC group, then every member floods its share; any k shares reconstruct, fewer reveal nothing. Provides (n - |attackers|)-anonymity for up to k-1 attackers at 10-100 kB/s throughput. Fixes the incentive problem that members of a DC group may refuse to forward.

title: Kadcast-NG: A Structured Broadcast Protocol for Blockchain Networks

title: SimpleX Agent Protocol
bitmessage_link: Gives each contact pair a ratcheted session with fresh queues, replacing Bitmessage's static-key per-address encryption with no forward secrecy.

title: SimpleX Messaging Protocol (SMP)
bitmessage_link: Server-held queue with receiver-chosen random addresses is the opposite design to Bitmessage's broadcast stream; admission control is by authenticated queue commands rather than proof-of-work.
note: Spec of SMP: recipient-created unidirectional simplex queues with separate sender/recipient IDs and keys, per-queue command auth, deniable client authentication, queue rotation, proxying. Hides: sender identity and sender-recipient link from the server (different IDs per direction), content. Leaks: message timing and sizes (padded), recipient IP to its own server.

title: TLS Beyond the Broker: Enforcing Fine-grained Security and Trust in Publish/Subscribe Environments for IoT

title: CoCoA: Concurrent Continuous Group Key Agreement
bitmessage_link: none direct

title: DeCAF: Decentralizable Continuous Group Key Agreement with Fast Healing
bitmessage_link: Decentralised group key agreement fits flooded or federated networks with no central sequencer.
note: DeCAF: decentralisable concurrent CGKA with fast healing (users heal after at most log(t) requests, t being the number of corrupted users) and low communication cost, usable without a central server to order updates; improves on CoCoA's healing speed.

title: Cryptographic Administration for Secure Group Messaging
bitmessage_link: Chans in Bitmessage have no membership control; A-CGKA is the formal answer.

title: Groove: Flexible Metadata-Private Messaging
bitmessage_link: Fixes the Bitmessage-relevant gaps of round-based systems: messages to offline buddies, multiple devices, low mobile cost, via oblivious delegation.

title: Hybrid Public Key Encryption
bitmessage_link: Modern replacement for Bitmessage's ECIES to a static recipient key; still static-key, so forward secrecy must come from the surrounding protocol.
note: Standard KEM-DEM public-key encryption (DHKEM, KDF, AEAD) with base, PSK, auth modes; used by MLS for TreeKEM node encryption; sender authentication in auth mode but no forward secrecy of the recipient key.

title: Mixnet optimization methods
bitmessage_link: Treats mixnet parameters as an optimisation problem; shows poor parameter choices give little or no protection.

title: An Event Mesh for Event Driven IoT Applications.

bitmessage_link: none direct

title: MARSHAL: Messaging with Asynchronous Ratchets and Signatures for faster HeALing
bitmessage_link: none direct

bitmessage_link: Provides the vocabulary to say that a static key never heals (infinite healing time).

title: Universally Composable End-to-End Secure Messaging
bitmessage_link: Composable definition of the properties a ratcheted channel gives, against which static-key designs can be compared.
note: UC model of Signal end-to-end secure messaging: an ideal functionality for messaging with a PKI and untrusted server against an adversary that controls the network and adaptively, momentarily compromises parties; captures Signal's forward secrecy and recovery of security and the exact conditions under which they break; decomposes Signal into PKI, continuous key exchange, epoch symmetric ratchets and AEAD functionalit

title: Rotatable Zero Knowledge Sets: Post Compromise Secure Auditable Dictionaries with application to Key Transparency
bitmessage_link: Post-compromise security for the key directory itself, the analogue of PCS for the session keys.
note: Rotatable zero-knowledge sets: append-only ZK sets for privacy-preserving key transparency that can restore privacy after a server compromise (post-compromise security of the directory) while keeping auditability.

title: Online Website Fingerprinting: Evaluating Website Fingerprinting Attacks on Tor in the Real World
bitmessage_link: Calibrates how much real-world traffic analysis threat remains for onion-service based messengers.
note: Evaluates fingerprinting on the live Tor network with a mix of user-like conditions and finds real-world accuracy lower than laboratory results but still meaningful. Adversary: passive local observer in the wild (no lab control).

title: CIP-83: Encrypted Transaction Message/Comment Metadata
bitmessage_link: Passphrase-shared encrypted message resembles a Bitmessage chan secret, but on a transparent ledger.
note: Symmetric encryption of the CIP-20 message under a shared passphrase (default value public in the spec). Hides content from non-holders of the passphrase; sender, recipient addresses and timing remain public; not a recipient-hiding design.

title: The Key Lattice Framework for Concurrent Group Messaging
bitmessage_link: Group key management over pairwise channels, matching deployments built from pairwise ratchets.
note: Key lattice framework: a key-management layer for concurrent group messaging over secure pairwise channels, with simpler game-based definitions combining forward secrecy and post-compromise security into directional notions; handles concurrent updates natively.

title: Single-Server Private Information Retrieval with Sublinear Amortized Time

title: Secure Messaging with Strong Compromise Resilience, Temporal Privacy, and Immediate Decryption
bitmessage_link: Temporal privacy (old messages stay private even if later keys leak) combined with immediate decryption is the design goal for out-of-order, store-and-forward delivery.
note: First provably secure messaging protocol achieving at once strong resilience to fine-grained compromise, temporal privacy and immediate decryption with constant-size overhead, in the post-quantum setting; introduces a new offline-deniability definition that the protocol meets when combined with a post-quantum offline-deniable initial key exchange.

title: Formal Analysis of Session-Handling in Secure Messaging: Lifting Security from Sessions to Conversations
bitmessage_link: Conversation-level (not session-level) forward secrecy and PCS, the level that matters for a multi-device user of a store-and-forward system.
note: Formal analysis of the session-handling layer (Sesame) above the Double Ratchet: shows experimentally that PCS can be violated in Signal by a clone attacker even with the Double Ratchet because merging multiple ratchet chains into one conversation lets the attacker's session persist; designs a fix (and a Tamarin-verified model) restoring FS and PCS at the conversation level.

title: FrodoPIR: Simple, Scalable, Single-Server Private Information Retrieval
bitmessage_link: Practical lattice PIR for mailbox-style retrieval instead of broadcast.

title: Publishing Asynchronous Event Times with Pufferfish Privacy
note: We show that perturbation of event timestamps or adding fake events following carefully chosen distributions can address these privacy concerns.

title: Strongly Anonymous Ratcheted Key Exchange
bitmessage_link: Closest theory to merging Bitmessage-style recipient privacy (key privacy, trial decryption) with ratcheted session keys.
note: Defines anonymity (hiding metadata about participants) for ratcheted key exchange under continuous, temporary exposure of user secrets, the first use of RKE to obtain strong anonymity guarantees under such exposure, and gives a strongly anonymous RKE construction alongside forward secrecy and post-compromise security.

title: Continuous Authentication in Secure Messaging
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage addresses bind keys by hash but offer no ongoing authentication step; this adds authentication that heals.
note: Authentication Steps extension for Signal-like protocols: continuous authentication during a session using users' long-term secrets (no out-of-band channel needed), guaranteeing authenticity while long-term secrets stay uncompromised, strengthening post-compromise security and allowing after-the-fact detection of long-term secret compromise; formal definition, general construction, proof and prototype.

title: ERC-5564: Stealth Addresses

title: Clarion: Anonymous Communication from Multiparty Shuffling Protocols

Extension to k servers secure against k-1 malicious ones with costlier preprocessing.

title: The Superlinearity Problem in Post-Quantum Blockchains
bitmessage_link: Theoretical limit for using proof-of-work as spam control in a post-quantum network.
note: Shows proof-of-work can be undermined by quantum computation even when all primitives are post-quantum: any puzzle with a superlinear quantum speedup (e.g. Grover) creates incentive incompatibility, and a puzzle must scale linearly in work for quantum and classical solvers to be safe. Gives constructions/impossibilities for post-quantum-sound puzzles.

title: Exploring the Effects of Multicast Communication on DDS Performance
note: The Data Distribution Service (DDS) is an Object Management Group (OMG) standard for high-performance and real-time systems.

title: Fuzzy Message Detection (Penumbra protocol specification)
bitmessage_link: Production adaptation of Beck et al.'s FMD for a shielded chain; the fix for scanning that Bitmessage lacks, with explicit leakage when the false-positive rate is wrong.
note: Deployed-chain specification of FMD: receiver FMD (receiver picks false-positive rate) and sender FMD (S-FMD: sender picks a consensus-determined rate, so precision adapts to global message rate), construction with constant-size keys, dummy clues so every transaction has as many clues as outputs, threat model, and a parameter-considerations page on statistical attacks that exploit knowledge of total messages and true

title: Penumbra protocol: Fuzzy Message Detection (S-FMD) chapters and note ciphertexts
bitmessage_link: Detection keys let an untrusted server pre-filter outputs with a tunable false-positive rate, removing most of the full-chain trial decryption; the production design of what Beck et al. proposed.
note: Seven mdBook pages concatenated. Other slices hold 2022-penumbra-fmd and 2022-penumbra-fmd-spec variants.

title: Penumbra protocol specification: addresses, detection keys, fuzzy message detection, memos and note ciphertexts
bitmessage_link: Applies fuzzy message detection to ledger outputs; a middle path between full trial-decrypt (Bitmessage) and tags.
note: Shielded chain whose addresses carry a detection key; senders attach fuzzy-message-detection clues so a delegated detection server can filter transactions for a user with no false negatives and a user-chosen false-positive rate (a tunable precision/anonymity trade-off). Note ciphertexts and memos are encrypted; sender, recipient and amounts hidden on-chain. Leaks: a detection entity given several detection keys can l

title: Strong Anonymity for Mesh Messaging
bitmessage_link: Anonymous messaging over phone-to-phone mesh networks without Internet, the setting where flooding (Bitmessage-style) is natural; shows how to add strong anonymity.
note: Cost model: 200 users each sending every 30 s under pessimistic crowd density; more than 3,000 users each sending every minute under more realistic assumptions. Trust: no central server; global passive observers of the mesh.

title: Total Eclipse of the Heart - Disrupting the InterPlanetary File System
bitmessage_link: Kademlia peer tables are eclipsed with cheap IDs; any DHT discovery used by a flooding messenger inherits this.
note: Eclipse attacks on IPFS nodes and content using a Kademlia/libp2p peer-table weakness, with low resource use. Adversary: attacker able to create many peer IDs close to the victim in key space, with limited bandwidth.

title: An Ambient Intelligence approach to provide secure and trusted Pub/Sub messaging systems in IoT environments
note: Trust and security layer for pub/sub messaging in IoT environments.

title: A New Approach to a Self-Organizing Federation of MQTT Brokers
note: A new variant for MQ Telemetry Transport, providing a well-structured mechanism for building and orchestrating the federation of brokers, and demonstrating that the protocol can easily provide flexible reliability with low complexity.

title: Ricochet Protocol v3 (Tor v3 onion services)
bitmessage_link: Peer-to-peer over Tor; no admission control other than contact approval (versus Bitmessage's PoW).
note: Wire protocol over Tor connection: packet/channel layers, contact request, chat channels, proof-of-possession of onion key. Content and identities hidden from network; each side learns the other's onion address after acceptance.

title: Hydra: Practical Metadata Security for Contact Discovery, Messaging, and Dialing
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.
note: Cost model: periodically (for example every ten minutes) built latency-aware, padded, onion-encrypted circuits used for connectionless contact requests and text; latency lower by an order of magnitude than round-based mixnet messengers; circuits upgradable to voice with slightly reduced anonymity. Trust: global observers, some malicious relays. Cited version is the SECRYPT 2021 paper.

title: A Survey on Anonymous Communication Systems with a Focus on Dining Cryptographers Networks
bitmessage_link: Survey of DC-net variants and what each trades for scalability and disruption resistance.
note: Cost model: survey, no new numbers. Useful for the DC-net family tree (Herbivore, Dissent, Verdict, Riposte, PriFi).

title: SimpleX Chat Protocol
bitmessage_link: Groups without Bitmessage-style chans: membership is decentralised in clients, not shared by a passphrase.
note: Application message format for direct and group chat on top of SMP/agent: groups are client-side meshes of pairwise connections, no server group state. Hides: group membership from servers.

title: SimpleX: messaging and application platform
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt recipient ambiguity with unlinkable per-contact queues addressed by random IDs; no global broadcast so bandwidth is O(own messages), at the cost of trusting that sender and recipient relays do n
note: Overview of SimpleX: no user identifiers, unidirectional per-contact queues on relays, 2-hop onion private routing. Hides: relationship from servers (separate queues per contact, no global ID), content (E2EE), sender IP from recipient's relay (private routing). Does not hide: timing and queue activity from a colluding relay pair; recipient IP from its own relay.

title: SimpleX Push Notifications
bitmessage_link: Mobile wake-up without polling a flood; Bitmessage has no mobile or push story.
note: Design of push notification delivery through APNS via notification server holding a per-queue token, without learning contacts or content. Leaks to Apple/notification server: device token and notification timing.

title: SimpleX File Transfer Protocol (XFTP)
bitmessage_link: Out-of-band bulk transfer avoids flooding large objects to every node as Bitmessage must.
note: Large file transfer by splitting into encrypted chunks stored on independent relays, retrieved with one-time descriptions sent in-band. Hides: file content, link between chunks (different servers, per-chunk keys). Leaks chunk sizes.

title: Privacy-Preserving Spam-Protected Gossip-Based Routing
note: Companion paper presenting RLN spam protection for gossip-based routing (the Waku2 relay).

title: WAKU-RLN-RELAY: Privacy-Preserving Peer-to-Peer Economic Spam Protection
note: Rate-limiting-nullifier spam protection for a GossipSub-based anonymous relay, with economic slashing.

title: Multicast Encryption in the Streamr Network
note: End-to-end multicast encryption and key distribution for a decentralised pub/sub network with untrusted relay nodes.

title: Waku: A Family of Modular P2P Protocols For Secure & Censorship-Resistant Communication
note: Overview of the Waku protocol family: libp2p-GossipSub relay plus store, filter and light-push.

title: SimpleX Chat Security Assessment (Trail of Bits, 2022-11-03)
bitmessage_link: Contrast: Bitmessage has no commissioned audit; this is the model for audited protocols in this wave.
note: One person-week review (Oct 2022) of SimpleX Chat: four findings (X3DH secrets not passed through HKDF, incorrect pad/unpad for long/short messages, key material in unpinned memory). Implementation and cryptography audit, not an analysis of the metadata claims.

title: Probabilistic Edge Multicast Routing for the XRP Network
note: Probabilistic multicast routing at the edge to replace XRPL flooding; precursor to the GossipSub-on-XRPL work.

title: Transparency Dictionaries with Succinct Proofs of Correct Operation
bitmessage_link: Directory-auditing building block; Bitmessage avoids a directory by self-certifying addresses.
note: Verdict: a transparency dictionary (untrusted service keeps a label-value map used for end-to-end-encryption key lookup) that proves publicly verifiably that every read and authorised update was executed correctly; composes indexed Merkle trees (SNARK-friendly) with the Phalanx SNARK for amortised constant-size proofs; scales to millions of labels with modest overhead.

title: 32/RLN-V1 (Rate Limit Nullifier)
bitmessage_link: Rate-limiting nullifier construction with Shamir secret sharing in a Merkle membership proof; the anonymous-credential rate limiting used instead of PoW.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: 53/WAKU2-X3DH
bitmessage_link: X3DH key agreement for Waku one-to-one sessions; gives forward secrecy with pre-key bundles, absent in Bitmessage.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: Noise sessions in Waku for 1-to-1 communication
bitmessage_link: Derives rendezvous content topics from handshake secrets, similar in spirit to Briar's BRP and Bitmessage's tag-based lookup.
note: Noise handshake-based session setup for 1:1 channels over Waku content topics with deterministic topic derivation and optional QR pairing.

title: TreeSync: Authenticated Group Management for Messaging Layer Security
bitmessage_link: Membership integrity and authenticated group state are exactly what chan passphrases do not provide.
note: Formalises TreeSync, MLS's group-integrity and authentication layer (authenticated tree of members and keys); gives a verified F* implementation and proves that group members agree on the tree and that only authorised members change it; identifies flaws in early drafts' state authentication.

title: Anonymity of NIST PQC Round 3 KEMs
bitmessage_link: First systematic answer to whether post-quantum KEM ciphertexts hide the recipient key.
note: Analyses ANO-CCA of all Round-3 KEMs: NTRU, BIKE, FrodoKEM, NTRU LPRime and SIKE are anonymous in the QROM; Classic McEliece needs a strongly disjoint-simulatable PKE; HQC fails for two of three parameter sets in the then-current design; Kyber and Saber had a gap in the QROM IND-CCA proof. Supersedes ePrint 2021/741.

title: zkBridge: Trustless Cross-chain Bridges Made Practical
note: Zero-knowledge proofs of consensus let a destination chain verify source-chain events without a trusted relayer.

title: Secure Hierarchical Deterministic Wallet Supporting Stealth Address
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage addresses are static and the public key is looked up by everyone; stealth/one-time addresses give per-message recipient keys, at the cost that the recipient must scan (an ECDH per candidate) unless a tag or detection key short-cu
note: First formal syntax and security model for HD wallets that also support stealth addresses, with a construction secure against derived-key exposure.

title: OpenPubSub: Supporting Large Semantic Content Spaces in Peer-to-Peer Publish/Subscribe Systems for the Internet of Multimedia Things
note: Zaarour et al.: OpenPubSub, semantic content-space P2P pub/sub (IEEE IoT-J).

title: Formal Security Definition of Metadata-Private Messaging
bitmessage_link: Formal game for metadata-private messaging; basis for judging claims such as Bitmessage's.
note: Cost model: none; gives a complete definition of metadata-private messaging that accounts for compromised friends and describes a compromised-friend attack variant against Addra-style deployments (their Anysphere app). Slug follows the other collector's copy (same file).

title: ZIP 231: Memo Bundles
bitmessage_link: Addresses the scan-cost vs message-size trade-off that Bitmessage also faces.
note: Draft to replace the fixed 512-byte memo with variable-length, separately-encrypted memo bundles so shielded transactions can carry larger messages without scanning cost for non-recipients.

title: A Lattice-based Publish-Subscribe Communication Protocol using Accelerated Homomorphic Encryption Primitives
bitmessage_link: Cost data for attribute-policy matching on encrypted pub/sub messages.
note: GPU acceleration of lattice KP-ABE encryption and homomorphic evaluation for pub/sub: 2.1x (encrypt) and 13.2x (homomorphic evaluation) faster than CPU on an i9, supporting up to 128 attributes.

title: Traceable mixnets
bitmessage_link: Tracing of mixed items for accountability, relevant to abuse handling in metadata-private systems.
note: Cost model: mixnet variant that selectively reveals chosen input-output associations (tracing) while keeping the rest hidden; motivated by e-voting. No messaging cost numbers; relevant to accountability and abuse handling.

title: Pantheon: Private Retrieval from Public Key-Value Store
bitmessage_link: Key-value lookup by tag is the retrieval primitive for a topic-addressed Bitmessage replacement.
note: Single-round private lookup in a public key-value store, 93x lower server-side latency than the prior state of the art through refined cryptography and massive parallelism; no numbers recorded beyond that.

title: Formal verification of the pub-sub blockchain interoperability protocol using stochastic timed automata
note: In recent times, the research on blockchain interoperability has gained momentum, enabling the entities from different heterogeneous blockchain networks to communicate with each other seamlessly.

title: Practically-exploitable Cryptographic Vulnerabilities in Matrix
bitmessage_link: Shows that federated-server mediation of group key distribution is a weaker trust base than Bitmessage's passphrase chans, but with server-visible metadata that Bitmessage's flood avoids.
note: Several practically-exploitable attacks by a malicious homeserver on Matrix and Element end-to-end encryption, invalidating its confidentiality and authentication claims (insecure-by-design pieces, protocol confusion, missing domain separation, implementation bugs across Olm, Megolm, key backup, key sharing and verification). The server sees room membership, senders, timing and sizes by design.

title: Fork-Resilient Continuous Group Key Agreement
bitmessage_link: Decentralised/unreliable delivery causes forks; a Bitmessage-style flood network inherits that problem.
note: Defines fork-resilient CGKA: after the group state forks (diverging histories from server or network failures), members can re-merge safely; shows MLS-like protocols cannot recover safely and proposes a fork-resilient construction using key-update and commit structure.

title: Using publish/subscribe for message routing in mobile environments
note: MFT-PubSub is a purely reactive solution for mobility in a publish/subscribe system without any kind of limits on the mobility patterns of the nodes, and is compared with AODV, a routing protocol for mobile ad hoc networking.

title: Advancing iMessage security: iMessage Contact Key Verification
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage avoids a key directory by embedding the key hash in the address; the cost is no human-readable names. Key transparency is how directory-based systems close the same trust gap.
note: Key transparency for the iMessage key directory: a verifiable log lets devices detect a malicious or compromised directory serving the wrong keys; users get automatic verification plus an out-of-band check; claims detection (not prevention) of key-directory attacks.

title: MixFlow: Assessing Mixnets Anonymity with Contrastive Architectures and Semantic Network Information
bitmessage_link: Flow-correlation attack on Poisson-mixing designs: shows delay and cover alone do not stop end-to-end linking.
note: Cost model: attack; about 90 percent accuracy correlating chat flows even with cover traffic of 60 packets per minute and Poisson delay of 50 s.

title: On the Cost of Post-Compromise Security in Concurrent Continuous Group-Key Agreement
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Examines the cost of post-compromise security in concurrent CGKA: sequential TreeKEM updates need all users to process previous updates; later TreeKEM versions allow concurrent updates at communication overhead linear in the number of concurrent updaters, and the paper gives bounds on what PCS costs under concurrency.

title: Basalt: A Rock-Solid Byzantine-Tolerant Peer Sampling for Very Large Decentralized Networks
note: Byzantine-tolerant peer sampling for very large decentralized networks, a membership primitive for gossip.

title: WhatsUpp with Sender Keys? Analysis, Improvements and Security Proofs
bitmessage_link: Sender Keys is the deployed model closest to a chan: one symmetric key per sender and no healing.
note: First formal analysis of the Sender Keys protocol (used by WhatsApp and Signal groups): new security model for Sender Keys-like protocols integrating two-party messaging, proof of a form of forward secrecy, identification of shortcomings (notably the lack of post-compromise security) and a practical improved protocol with proofs.

title: The Messaging Layer Security (MLS) Protocol
bitmessage_link: The group answer Bitmessage lacks: chans there share one passphrase-derived key forever, so membership change means a new key for everyone and no PCS. MLS gives per-epoch keys and cheap add/remove.
note: Asynchronous group key establishment with a ratchet tree (TreeKEM): O(log n) updates, forward secrecy and post-compromise security for groups, authenticated membership changes via Add/Update/Remove proposals and Commits, epoch-based key schedule; claims confidentiality, integrity, authentication, membership agreement, asynchronicity, PCS; leaves open metadata hiding and concurrency/robustness limits.

title: Cumulative Memory Lower Bounds for Randomized and Quantum Computation
bitmessage_link: Theory for swapping Bitmessage's compute PoW for a memory-hard one that stays hard under quantum speedups.
note: Proves cumulative memory complexity lower bounds for randomized and quantum circuits (extending to quantum the classical pebbling-based memory-hardness proofs); supports using memory-hard puzzles when a quantum adversary is considered, because Grover does not compress cumulative memory-time.

title: Formal Verification of a Post-Quantum Signal Protocol with Tamarin
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Tamarin model of a post-quantum variant of Signal (PQ handshake and ratchet) checking secrecy, forward secrecy and post-compromise security against a Dolev-Yao adversary with KEM-based replacements; reports no attacks in the modelled variant.

title: ethp2psim: Evaluating and deploying privacy-enhanced peer-to-peer routing protocols for the Ethereum network
bitmessage_link: Tooling for comparing source-hiding gossip variants; relevant when estimating how a flood-based messenger leaks origin.
note: Simulator to evaluate and deploy privacy-enhanced P2P transaction routing protocols (Dandelion++-like, k-anonymous variants) for Ethereum against first-spy style adversaries. Adversary: passive network observers and spy coalitions placed at configurable positions.

title: Lattice-Based Blind Signatures: Short, Efficient, and Round-Optimal
bitmessage_link: Sets the floor for post-quantum anonymous token size, orders of magnitude above a 64-byte ECDSA signature.
note: Two-round blind signature, signature 22 KB, transcript as small as 60 KB; standard lattice assumptions (Ring/Module-SIS, LWE, NTRU). Compare roughly 45 KB for Agrawal et al. and about 100 KB for del Pino-Katsumata.

title: Self-Managed Federation of MQTT Brokers with Dynamic Topology Control
note: Abstract not retrieved; included on title and venue (Journal of Computer Science).

title: Oblivious Homomorphic Encryption
bitmessage_link: Removes the need for every recipient to download and trial-decrypt the whole board, which is Bitmessage's recipient-ambiguity mechanism, while keeping the server blind to who each message is for; stronger than a fuzzy filter but needs FHE o
note: OHE: an FHE service separates the computation spaces of multiple clients while staying blind about whom each result belongs to; used as a generic route to OMR-like services. No benchmark numbers recorded here.

title: ASMesh: Anonymous and Secure Messaging in Mesh Networks Using Stronger, Anonymous Double Ratchet
bitmessage_link: A direct successor of Bitmessage's setting (untrusted relays, no server) that adds a ratchet and unlinkable headers.
note: Messaging for mesh networks (no central relay; clients relay ciphertexts, for scenarios such as mass protests in censored networks): a new security model capturing forward and post-compromise security as well as forward and post-compromise anonymity, stronger confidentiality goals possible because of delay and distribution, and ASMesh, a provably secure protocol built on a stronger anonymous Double Ratchet; motivated

title: BIP 352: Silent Payments
bitmessage_link: Scan-all recipient model on a public ledger, with the scan key delegable for bandwidth.
note: Static receiver address; sender derives unique output script from input keys; the receiver scans all eligible transactions with its scan key (delegable to a scan-only server). No notification message. Hides relationship and recipient from observers; sender inputs are public.

title: Poster: No safety in numbers: traffic analysis of sealed-sender groups in Signal
bitmessage_link: Concrete traffic-analysis limit on sender hiding without batching or cover traffic; Bitmessage's flood avoids recipient-side leakage but is global-adversary timing-exposed.
note: Extends the Martiny et al. statistical disclosure attack on Signal's sealed sender from pairs to whole group conversations: the server, seeing who receives messages and the receipts, can recover group membership. Sealed sender hides the sender per message only.

title: Towards Scalable Cross-Chain Messaging
note: Scalable cross-chain messaging between blockchains.

title: Quarantined-TreeKEM: a Continuous Group Key Agreement for MLS, Secure in Presence of Inactive Users
bitmessage_link: Inactive members are common in asynchronous delivery; relevant to store-and-forward groups.
note: Quarantined-TreeKEM: handles inactive users who would otherwise block PCS and FS in TreeKEM by putting them in quarantine; keeps the same security level for active members with limited extra cost.

title: Real-World Deniability in Messaging
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage's non-repudiable signatures are the extreme case; this paper argues even 'deniable' protocols give little practical deniability.
note: Model of real-world deniability that covers the whole messaging system (not only the cryptographic protocol); concludes Signal and DKIM-signed email give no practical deniability; also finds, in 140 Swiss court cases, that no judgment considered deniability.

title: Zenoh: Unifying Communication, Storage and Computation from the Cloud to the Microcontroller
note: Zenoh a Pub/Sub-/Query protocol that unifies data at rest, data in motion and computations is introduced that runs and perform on constrained as well as on high end networks and hardware.

title: Keeping Up with the KEMs: Stronger Security Notions for KEMs and Automated Analysis of KEM-based protocols
bitmessage_link: The KEM binding properties are what the PQXDH verification found missing; relevant to any post-quantum upgrade of static-key encryption.
note: Stronger security notions for KEMs (binding of the shared secret to ciphertext and public key; the KEM binding property needed by PQXDH and similar protocols) and a symbolic analysis method (Tamarin) for protocols that use KEMs; shows relations between notions and applies them to protocols including Signal-style handshakes.

title: Pentest-Report Delta Chat Mail-Server Template & Libraries 02.2023 (MER-01)
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Audit of the chatmail/mail-server template and networking libraries; eight issues including unencrypted SQLite storage. Concerns the server side where all Delta Chat metadata resides.

title: ERC-6538: Stealth Meta-Address Registry
bitmessage_link: A public key directory for stealth keys; the discovery step that Bitmessage does with address-to-pubkey requests.
note: Canonical on-chain registry mapping a registrant to its stealth meta-address, so a sender can find the recipient's scan and spend keys without interaction.

title: Abuse Reporting for Metadata-Hiding Communication Based on Secret Sharing
bitmessage_link: Abuse reports in secret-sharing-based systems such as Express and Riposte.
note: Cost model: see paper.

title: Messenger End-to-End Encryption Overview
bitmessage_link: Shows how a large service layers storage and history restore on a ratcheted pairwise design, the property trade-off Bitmessage's network-wide object retention embodies.
note: Messenger's default E2EE design: Signal Protocol sessions, group messages with Sender Keys over server-side fan-out, device registration, and a new server-side storage protocol for message history; claims content confidentiality and forward secrecy through hash ratchets for 1:1 and group sessions; the server still sees who communicates and when.

title: Farcaster Specifications (version 2023.11.15)
bitmessage_link: Public pub/sub-like feed replicated among hubs; useful as a non-private control for Bitmessage's private broadcast.
note: On-chain id registry plus signed messages replicated among hubs via CRDT sync. All protocol messages (casts, reactions, follows) are public; the spec contains no private-message type, so direct casts sit outside it. Hides nothing about sender, topic or timing.

title: Event-Driven Fabric Blockchain - ROS 2 Interface: Towards Secure and Auditable Teleoperation of Mobile Robots
note: Event-driven Hyperledger Fabric to ROS 2 interface for auditable robot teleoperation.

title: Mitigating Intersection Attacks in Anonymous Microblogging
bitmessage_link: Long-term intersection attacks on anonymous broadcast, which hit Bitmessage chans and any system with churn.
note: Cost model: protocol groups users into anonymity sets by publishing behaviour and gives each set a configurable communication schedule that trades latency against bandwidth; evaluated by simulating Twitter and Reddit publishing data; anonymity set degrades slowly under churn.

title: On the Inherent Anonymity of Gossiping
bitmessage_link: Direct theory for flood-vs-route: pure flooding from the source reveals the first contacted curious node; no gossip scheme beats eps = ln(f-1).
note: Source anonymity of gossip measured by eps-DP against f curious nodes. Thm 5 (universal lower bound): for any connected graph G of size n, f>1 curious nodes and any gossip protocol P, if P satisfies eps-DP against an average-case or worst-case adversary then eps >= ln(f-1); moreover if the vertex connectivity kappa(G) <= f, P cannot satisfy eps-DP with finite eps against a worst-case adversary. title: Scalable Private Signaling
bitmessage_link: Improves private signaling scalability.
note: Cost model: see paper.

title: Jami developer documentation: swarm conversations, Dynamic Routing Table (DRT), identifiers, connection manager and synchronization
bitmessage_link: Moves from DHT-stored messages (a global-ish store, like Bitmessage's flood in spirit) to member-only overlays, shrinking ambiguity but exposing IPs to members.
note: Conversation as a signed Git-like Merkle DAG synchronised directly between members, with a DHT used for rendezvous and invitations and a DRT overlay among members. Hides content (TLS and per-account certificates); members learn each other's IP, DHT nodes see account-hash lookups and timing. Messages now need a live peer connection, not DHT storage.

title: Secure and Dynamic Publish/Subscribe: LCMsec
note: We propose LCMsec, a brokerless, decentralised Publish/Subscribe protocol.

title: Scaling Mobile Private Contact Discovery to Billions of Users
bitmessage_link: Contact discovery for billions of users using PSI/PIR hybrids.
note: Cost model: see paper; targets WhatsApp-scale user bases.

title: Pudding: Private User Discovery in Anonymity Networks
note: In this paper we propose Pudding, a novel private user discovery protocol that allows a user to be contacted on an anonymity network knowing only their

title: Implementation and Evaluation of the Control Mechanism Among Distributed MQTT Brokers
note: The Distributed MQTT broker by data Link look-up for Traffic reduction (DMLT) is proposed as a new routing mechanism aimed at layer-2 based control and invokes a traffic reduction and simplified transfer by an independent flow.

title: Anonymity Analysis of the Umbra Stealth Address Scheme on Ethereum
bitmessage_link: Heuristics identify the real recipient for about half of Umbra stealth payments; measured anonymity of a deployed receiver-scanning scheme (recipient scans announcements by trial).
note: Preprint; discusses linear scanning cost and signalling as remedies.

title: Quantum Resistance and the Signal Protocol
bitmessage_link: Context for the threat that recorded Bitmessage ciphertexts (every node stores them for days) face from harvest-now-decrypt-later.
note: Announces PQXDH: hybrid X25519 plus CRYSTALS-Kyber (later ML-KEM) key agreement at session start to resist harvest-now-decrypt-later; explains that authentication remains classical.

title: Data Availability Sampling in Ethereum: Analysis of P2P Networking Requirements
note: Analyses networking requirements of DAS and the role of GossipSub and DHT-based dissemination.

title: Verification of GossipSub in ACL2s
note: Verification of GossipSub properties in the ACL2s theorem prover.

title: Lattice-based Commit-Transferrable Signatures and Applications to Anonymous Credentials
bitmessage_link: Candidate admission credential in place of per-object proof-of-work.
note: Commit-transferrable signature primitive plus lattice NIZKPoK gives a modular anonymous credential with smaller proofs than earlier lattice constructions; post-quantum under SIS/LWE.

title: Trellis: Robust and Scalable Metadata-private Anonymous Broadcast
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.
note: Cost model: routing mixnet with anonymous routing tokens for verifiable random paths and lightweight blame protocols. With 64 servers over four regions, 220 bits per second with 100,000 users; 320 bits per second with 128 servers; 100 to 1000x slower than Tor. Trust: a fraction of servers may be malicious; guarantees availability for honest users.

title: TreePIR: Sublinear-Time and Polylog-Bandwidth Private Information Retrieval from DDH
bitmessage_link: Replaces broadcast-and-trial-decrypt with indexed private retrieval: the recipient fetches only its slots and the server learns nothing about which; works only if the recipient can compute or look up the slot (a rendezvous or mailbox index)
note: Two-server PIR with sublinear amortized server time and polylogarithmic bandwidth from DDH; outperforms prior two-server schemes in practice.

title: OPTIKS: An Optimized Key Transparency System
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: OPTIKS: a full-featured key transparency system optimised for scalability (simpler and faster than prior designs, smaller storage overhead, crash-tolerant scalable server architecture) while keeping strong security and privacy notions; addresses real-world deployment issues.

title: Hintless Single-Server Private Information Retrieval
bitmessage_link: Stateless lattice PIR suitable for a client that cannot keep per-server state.
note: PIR with no client-side hint (and no offline preprocessing) from LWE with a modest communication increase compared with SimplePIR-style schemes; post-quantum.

title: A Performance Study on the Throughput and Latency of Zenoh, MQTT, Kafka, and DDS
note: In this study, we compare the performance of the new-generation communication protocol Zenoh with the widely-used MQTT, Kafka, and DDS.

title: Group Oblivious Message Retrieval
bitmessage_link: Addresses chans/group delivery without flooding; recipient set hidden by key-private encryption.
note: OMR for multi-recipient messages; builds the first lattice-based key-private multi-recipient encryption (KP-MRE). Reported parameters (D,Q,t)=(2^15,~2850,65537) with 612-byte payload. Assumptions: ring/module LWE.

title: How Can AI be Distributed in the Computing Continuum? Introducing the Neural Pub/Sub Paradigm
note: This paper proposes the neural publish/subscribe paradigm, a novel approach to orchestrating AI workflows in large-scale distributed AI systems in the computing continuum.

title: VeraSel: Verifiable Random Selection for Mixnets Construction
bitmessage_link: Verifiable random selection of mix nodes for stratified topologies, removing the need for a trusted directory.
note: Cost model: verifiable randomness per epoch; compares overhead for building layers in large mixnets; no user-capacity numbers.

title: Parakeet: Practical Key Transparency for End-to-End Encrypted Messaging
bitmessage_link: A directory-based answer to the key-distribution problem that Bitmessage avoids by having no directory (addresses encode keys) at the cost of out-of-band address exchange.
note: Production-oriented key transparency (built around Meta's AKD used by WhatsApp): a privacy-preserving verifiable username-to-key map plus consistency protocol so a malicious server cannot silently serve false keys. Protects key authenticity (content security); the server still sees lookups and the contact graph by timing.

title: Topiary: Fast, Scalable Publish/Subscribe for Peer-to-Peer (D)Apps
note: Learns a per-topic p2p topology by multi-armed-bandit neighbour selection; compared against GossipSub-style baselines for dApp pub/sub.

title: Device-Oriented Group Messaging: A Formal Cryptographic Analysis of Matrix' Core
bitmessage_link: Formal limits for symmetric sender-key group ratchets, relevant to Bitmessage chans which have no ratchet at all.
note: First formal model of Matrix group messaging (Device-Oriented Group Messaging): Matrix achieves confidentiality and authentication provided it introduces authenticated group membership; its state-sharing features (history sharing, account recovery) conflict with forward secrecy and post-compromise security. Content/session analysis; metadata out of scope.

title: ComDeX: a context-aware federated platform for IoT-enhanced communities
note: Abstract not retrieved; included on title and venue (17th ACM International Conference on Distributed and Event‐Based Systems (DEBS)).

title: Don't be Dense: Efficient Keyword PIR for Sparse Databases
bitmessage_link: Sparse key space is exactly the situation of a tag or topic space far larger than the set of messages present.
note: SparsePIR: keyword PIR over sparse key spaces with half the response overhead of prior keyword PIR and no linear-size client mapping; variants trade encoding time and small client state for smaller served databases.

title: Three Lessons From Threema: Analysis of a Secure Messenger
bitmessage_link: Deployed custom-crypto messenger analysed after 10+ years; Bitmessage's ad-hoc design faces similar risks.
note: Cryptographic analysis of Threema's custom protocols (client-server, end-to-end, device-to-device) finding several attacks and weaknesses after a decade of deployment; lessons on proprietary protocols and weak composition. Content and authentication focus; the Threema server sees metadata.

title: A Survey on Experimental Performance Evaluation of Data Distribution Service (DDS) Implementations
note: The Data Distribution Service (DDS) is a widely used communication specification for real-time mission-critical systems that follow the principles of publish-subscribe middleware.

title: An efficient confidentiality protection solution for pub/sub system
note: In this paper, we propose SBM (scalable blind matching), an effective confidentiality protection scheme for pub/sub systems.

title: BREPubSub: A Secure Publish-Subscribe Model using Blockchain and Re-encryption for IoT Data Sharing Management
note: Secure pub/sub for IoT data sharing using blockchain and re-encryption.

title: Implementation and Evaluation of LISP Publish/Subscribe
note: The design of future 6G network will push even further the convergence of different types of mobile networks, integrating space, aerial and terrestrial access.

title: Post-Quantum Privacy Pass via Post-Quantum Anonymous Credentials
bitmessage_link: Anonymous rate limiting is the post-quantum alternative to Bitmessage proof-of-work; the token size shows why it is hard to attach to every flooded object.
note: Anonymous credential from zkDilithium (a STARK-friendly Dilithium2 variant) plus zkSTARK proofs; token size trades 85-175 KB against generation time, verification 20-30 ms, verifier RAM under 5 MB; comparable to best post-quantum blind signatures (22-100 KB). Supports rate-limited Privacy Pass. Assumptions: module-LWE/SIS plus hash-based STARKs.

title: Post Quantum Fuzzy Stealth Signatures and Applications
bitmessage_link: Fuzzy detection is a middle path between trial-decrypting everything and full OMR.
note: Post-quantum stealth signatures with fuzzy matching (a tunable false-positive rate reduces the recipient's scanning set), built from lattices; applications include private payments and retrieval.

title: RFC 9474: RSA Blind Signatures
bitmessage_link: Token type for publicly verifiable anonymous admission.
note: RSABSSA blind signature scheme (RSA-PSS) with public verifiability. Adversary: malicious signer attempting to link signatures to signing sessions, and forger attempting one-more forgery.

title: RFC 9497: Oblivious Pseudorandom Functions (OPRFs) Using Prime-Order Groups
bitmessage_link: Primitive behind unlinkable tokens.
note: OPRF, VOPRF and POPRF over prime-order groups; building block for Privacy Pass and PSI. Adversary: malicious client or server, with verifiability to detect a key-switching server.

title: Unique-Path Identity Based Encryption With Applications to Strongly Secure Messaging
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Unique-Path IBE: a restricted hierarchical IBE sufficient for strongly secure messaging (strongly secure messaging protocols are equivalent to key-updatable KEMs, all prior constructions rely on adaptive unbounded-depth HIBE) with much better efficiency, enabling optimal-security messaging without the prohibitive HIBE cost.

title: SoK: Metadata-Protecting Communication Systems
bitmessage_link: Best single comparison table of 31 systems (mixnets, DC-nets, PIR, TEE) with their cost and trust assumptions; the reference for this slice.
note: Cost model: unified view of 31 systems against global network adversaries; compares trust assumptions, latency, scale. Use this as the cross-check for numbers quoted elsewhere in the catalog.

title: On the Anonymity of Peer-To-Peer Network Anonymity Schemes Used by Cryptocurrencies
bitmessage_link: Quantifies how little Dandelion-style stems and onion-routed payment paths hide, so stem-phase source hiding in a Bitmessage-like system should not be read as strong anonymity.
note: Bayesian framework giving per-transaction originator distributions; evaluates Dandelion, Dandelion++ and Lightning Network onion routing. Adversary: colluding nodes (1 to 15 percent, strategically placed) observing messages; finds Lightning Network 1 percent colluders identify the originator of about 50 percent of payments, and Dandelion anonymity set does not grow with network size.

title: Ruffle: Rapid 3-party shuffle protocols
bitmessage_link: Fast 3-party shuffle usable for mixing in MPC-based anonymous messaging.
note: Cost model: see paper.

title: The PQXDH Key Agreement Protocol (revision 3)
bitmessage_link: PQ session establishment that Bitmessage's static ECC keys lack.
note: Adds CRYSTALS-Kyber KEM to X3DH for post-quantum-protected initial key agreement; server-held prekey bundles. Content-only; Signal server knows account IDs and contact graph timing.

title: SimpleX security and threat model
bitmessage_link: Explicit adversary matrix; Bitmessage has none and its flooding model hides recipient only against non-global observers.
note: Threat model for SimpleX: what a single relay, colluding relays, a network observer and a compromised device can learn. States residual leaks: traffic correlation by global observer, IP exposure to own relay unless Tor, timing.

title: SimpleX Remote Control Protocol (XRCP)
bitmessage_link: none direct (multi-device handling absent in Bitmessage)
note: Protocol for a desktop to control a mobile app via authenticated, encrypted local channel with hybrid PQ KEM. Device-to-device; no network metadata concerns.

title: Post Quantum Sphinx
bitmessage_link: Post-quantum Sphinx variants (CSIDH-based NIKE and KEM Sphinx) for mixnets; fills the quantum gap in Bitmessage's static ECC keys.
note: Cost model: two public-key operations per hop; X25519 pair costs about 160-233 ns on the author's laptop, KEM variants cost more and packet headers grow. KEM Sphinx is adopted by Katzenpost.

title: Building a publish/subscribe information dissemination platform for hybrid mobile ad-hoc social networks over android devices
note: Building a publish/subscribe information dissemination platform for hybrid mobile ad-hoc social networks over android devices.

title: Revisiting BBS Signatures
bitmessage_link: Signature primitive for multi-show unlinkable credentials.
note: Security proof of BBS signatures in the algebraic group model with a tighter reduction; BBS underlies selective-disclosure anonymous credentials. Adversary: forger with chosen-message access in AGM.

title: Tor proposal 333: Vanguards lite
bitmessage_link: Default-on version of the guard-discovery defence.
note: Lightweight vanguards enabled by default for all clients: one extra layer of guard for non-onion circuits. Adversary: guard-discovery attacker with limited resources.

title: Tor proposal 340: Packed and fragmented relay messages
bitmessage_link: Shows the engineering price of larger post-quantum objects in a fixed-cell network.
note: Lets relay messages exceed one cell by packing and fragmentation; relay cell body 509 - 16 = 493 bytes (498 before), cell authentication digest grows from 4 to 14 bytes. Needed so post-quantum handshake messages (ML-KEM-768 key 1184 B) can cross circuits.

title: XRP-NDN overlay: Improving the Communication Efficiency of Consensus-Validation based Blockchains with an NDN-based Overlay
note: NDN-based overlay to cut XRPL consensus message flooding; sibling to the GossipSub work.

title: The Internals of Veilid: A New Distributed Application Framework
bitmessage_link: Dual-route compose of sender and receiver privacy replaces Bitmessage's flood-for-recipient-ambiguity.
note: Veilid design: DHT for private-route and value storage, safety routes (sender privacy) plus private routes (receiver privacy) composed so no node knows both ends. Hides sender and receiver network location from each other and from relays; no global-adversary claim.

title: BaseSAP: Modular Stealth Address Protocol for Programmable Blockchains
bitmessage_link: On-chain announcement and scan, closest ledger analogue to Bitmessage's tagged flood.
note: Modular base-layer stealth address protocol (basis of ERC-5564) with announcements on a contract, dual-key secp256k1 scheme, cost analysis and attack vectors against recipient privacy. Hides recipient behind stealth address; announcement metadata and funding are public.

title: Lotus: Serverless In-Transit Data Processing for Edge-based Pub/Sub
note: Publish-subscribe systems are a popular approach for edge-based IoT use cases: Heterogeneous, constrained edge devices can be integrated easily, with message routing logic offloaded to edge message brokers.

title: NOTRY: deniable messaging with retroactive avowal
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: NOTRY: deniable messaging where users can retroactively avow a conversation transcript (avowable designated-verifier proofs), at about 8x communication and computation overhead.

title: Secured and Cooperative Publish/Subscribe Scheme in Autonomous Vehicular Networks
note: Aiming at addressing security concerns in future AVs, in this paper, we develop SPAD, a secured framework to forbid free-riders and promote trustworthy data dissemination in collaborative autonomous driving.

title: XIP-42: Universal 'allow' and 'block' preferences
bitmessage_link: Recipient-side filtering as an alternative to Bitmessage's per-object proof-of-work.
note: Client-side consent lists (allowed/denied addresses), stored as an encrypted message on a user-preferences topic, to filter spam in a wallet-addressed inbox. Spam control is by recipient-side allow-list rather than sender cost.

title: Comparison of Middlewares in Edge-to-Edge and Edge-to-Cloud Communication for Distributed ROS2 Systems
note: The increased data transmission and number of devices involved in communications among distributed systems make it challenging yet significantly necessary to have an efficient and reliable networking middleware.

title: Piano: Extremely Simple, Single-Server PIR with Sublinear Server Computation
bitmessage_link: Sublinear per-message server work is what lets a mailbox server scale to a Bitmessage-sized pool; client keeps O(sqrt n) state.
note: First practical sublinear-time single-server PIR using only PRFs: amortized O~(sqrt n) server and client time, O(sqrt n) communication per query, sqrt n client storage. For a 100 GB database at 60 ms round trip, 73 ms response time, 40x-900x faster than prior single-server PIR.

title: Approaches to Conflict-free Replicated Data Types
note: This article provides solid coverage of the essential concepts of CRDT, clarifying some misconceptions that frequently occur, but also presents some novel insights gained from considerable experience in designing both specific CRDTs and approaches to CRDTs.

title: iMessage with PQ3: The new state of the art in quantum-secure messaging at scale
bitmessage_link: A production design for post-quantum PCS on an asynchronous channel; the rekey-period trade-off is the bandwidth-versus-healing choice any flooded network must make.
note: Hybrid post-quantum (Kyber-1024/ML-KEM plus P-256) initial key establishment and a periodic post-quantum rekeying inside an ECDH ratchet; claims post-quantum forward secrecy and post-compromise security (Level 3 on Apple's own scale), with ECDSA device signatures still classical; rekeying cadence is traded against message size.

title: Practical Post-Quantum Signatures for Privacy
bitmessage_link: Candidate group-signature or credential primitive for per-sender rate limiting.
note: Lattice signature with efficient protocols, aimed at privacy-preserving constructions such as anonymous credentials and group-style signatures, with concrete parameters smaller than earlier lattice proofs of possession.

title: Aztec documentation: private events, note discovery (tagging) and offchain message delivery
bitmessage_link: Moves from Bitmessage-style trial decryption to per-pair rolling tags, trading recipient privacy against the node for scan cost.
note: Private events encrypted to recipients; logs carry tag = poseidon2(shared_secret, index) so recipients query a node by tag instead of trial-decrypting; secret from arbitrary, address-derived, or non-interactive/interactive handshake; modes: onchain constrained/unconstrained or offchain. Hides content, and (with tags) which log belongs to whom to anyone lacking the secret; an onchain handshake reveals that a handshake

title: Looking AT the Blue Skies of Bluesky
note: Measurement of the Bluesky network including the relay and firehose data flows.

title: X-Wing: The Hybrid KEM You’ve Been Looking For
bitmessage_link: Practical hybrid KEM for replacing the classical ECDH step in static-key encryption.
note: X-Wing hybrid KEM from X25519 and ML-KEM-768 with a SHA3-256 combiner; proves classical IND-CCA security under the strong DH assumption in the ROM and post-quantum IND-CCA security if ML-KEM-768 is IND-CCA and SHA3-256 is a PRF (standard model), so it is secure if either component is; efficiency gains rely on the specific component choices and do not generalise.

title: Blending Different Latency Traffic With Beta Mixing
bitmessage_link: Lets latency-tolerant and latency-sensitive traffic share one mixnet, so slow traffic (Bitmessage-like email) pads fast traffic.
note: Cost model: mixes apply per-message delay parameters so users choose latency/anonymity per message; evaluated for anonymity gain of blending traffic classes.

title: Formal verification of the PQXDH Post-Quantum key agreement protocol for end-to-end secure messaging
bitmessage_link: State of the art for verifying PQ session setup in a deployed messenger.
note: ProVerif and CryptoVerif proofs of PQXDH including a KEM re-encapsulation attack that motivated spec changes. Content/session security only.

title: SoK: On the Security Goals of Key Transparency Systems
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Surveys the key transparency literature and gives the first cryptographically sound formalisation of KT as an ideal functionality, identifying security goals (including previously unstated ones) and comparing designs (CONIKS, SEEMless, Parakeet, OPTIKS, Merkle^2).

title: Consistency-or-Die: Consistency for Key Transparency
bitmessage_link: Decentralised, user-run consistency checking instead of trusted auditors.
note: Consistency-or-Die: a consistency protocol protecting a key transparency log against split-view attacks without small committees of known auditors, out-of-band channels or blockchains, using a randomly selected, initially undisclosed committee of users (VRFs, key-evolving signatures) to endorse the log view; users know whether they are consistent and stop using the log if not.

title: Bruisable Onions: Anonymous Communication in the Asynchronous Model
bitmessage_link: Asynchronous operation is the realistic setting for Bitmessage-like networks; prior provable bounds assume rounds.
note: First provably anonymous onion routing in the asynchronous (no synchronised rounds) model; bruisable onion encryption lets a relay damage a delayed onion so chronic delays make it undeliverable, blocking timing attacks. Removes the synchrony assumption underlying the trilemma and Ando et al.'s round-based bounds.

title: Respire: High-Rate PIR for Databases with Small Records
bitmessage_link: Small-record PIR matches the message-slot shape of a mailbox board, the regime a Bitmessage replacement would live in.
note: Tuned for small records such as message slots: 6.1 KB online communication to fetch one 256-byte record from over a million records (5.9x less than the best prior lattice scheme); batch queries use 3.4-7.1x less communication at 200-400 MB/s throughput.

title: Call Me By My Name: Simple, Practical Private Information Retrieval for Keyword Queries
bitmessage_link: Keyword PIR lets a recipient look up messages by tag or topic instead of slot number, the case that fits Bitmessage-style tag subscriptions.
note: ChalametPIR: converts any LWE index-PIR into keyword PIR using Binary Fuse filters, with at most 1.08x cost over the index scheme; 6x-11x faster and 3.75x-11.4x cheaper than prior keyword PIR.

title: The Art of Bonsai: How Well-Shaped Trees Improve the Communication Cost of MLS
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Improves MLS communication cost by choosing tree shapes: user add and tree expansion algorithms with better worst-case and average-case cost than the standard ones.

title: Rabbit-Mix: Robust Algebraic Anonymous Broadcast from Additive Bases
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.
note: Cost model: sender-anonymous broadcast with robustness and 100 percent delivery; about 3x fewer algebraic operations and less communication than Blinder, and removes Blinder's non-negligible failure probability. Trust: strong honest majority of servers.

title: Bots can Snoop: Uncovering and Mitigating Privacy Risks of Bots in Group Chats
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Finds chatbots in group chats read far more messages than needed and can link a user across groups (3.6 percent chance on joining a new group with bots); proposes SnoopGuard on top of MLS giving selective message access and sender anonymity toward bots at O(log n + m) sending cost.

title: Performance Comparison of ROS2 Middlewares for Multi-robot Mesh Networks in Planetary Exploration
note: Recent advancements in Multi-Robot Systems (MRS) and mesh network technologies pave the way for innovative approaches to explore extreme environments.

title: Pirates: Anonymous Group Calls over Fully Untrusted Infrastructure
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.
note: Cost model: single server supports three-member group calls from 11 concurrent users with mouth-to-ear latency under 365 ms. Trust: none; unobservability even if all servers are malicious.

title: On the Tight Security of the Double Ratchet
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Tight security bounds for the Double Ratchet in the multi-session setting, revisiting the Alwen-Coretti-Dodis modular decomposition; prior proofs gave guarantees that degrade with the number of interactions even in the single-session case; covers forward security, post-compromise security, adaptive state corruption, injections and out-of-order delivery.

title: K-Waay: Fast and Deniable Post-Quantum X3DH without Ring Signatures
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Fast deniable post-quantum X3DH that replaces ring signatures with a new 'split KEM' used for authentication; claims asynchrony, post-quantum security and deniability (in the sense of Brendel et al.) with much smaller message sizes than ring-signature constructions.

title: The Waku Network as Infrastructure for dApps
note: Architecture of the shared Waku network: relay routing and sharding, discovery, RLN rate limiting, services and incentives.

title: Scalability limitations of Kademlia DHTs when enabling Data Availability Sampling in Ethereum
note: Quantifies Kademlia limits for DAS propagation; the DHT alternative to gossip-based dissemination.

title: Impossibility Results for Post-Compromise Security in Real-World Communication Systems
bitmessage_link: Sets a ceiling on what PCS can mean in practice for users who copy keys between devices, as Bitmessage users must.
note: Proves impossibility results for post-compromise security at the end-user level: although ratcheting protocols (iMessage, WhatsApp, Signal) have been proven to achieve PCS at the protocol level, communication systems with the usability features users need (such as multi-device, backups or restoring a state) cannot provide PCS against a compromise of such state; formalises conditions under which end users can obtain P

title: VeriSimplePIR: Verifiability in SimplePIR at No Online Cost for Honest Servers
bitmessage_link: A message board server that is malicious rather than semi-honest can otherwise tamper per-client; relevant to untrusted mailbox nodes.
note: Adds verifiability to SimplePIR so a malicious server cannot equivocate on the database or run selective-failure attacks, at no extra online cost when the server is honest.

title: WhisPIR: Stateless Private Information Retrieval with Low Communication
bitmessage_link: Replaces broadcast-and-trial-decrypt with indexed private retrieval: the recipient fetches only its slots and the server learns nothing about which; works only if the recipient can compute or look up the slot (a rendezvous or mailbox index)
note: Fully stateless PIR for ephemeral clients that appear with only public parameters; needs much less communication than other stateless lattice PIR and is slower only than SimplePIR and HintlessPIR on large entries. Suits frequently updated boards.

title: Decentralized Reliability Estimation for Low-Latency Mixnets
bitmessage_link: Lets mixnet clients estimate node reliability in a stateless per-packet-routed network (Nym).
note: Cost model: decentralised measurement using VRF-based sampling; no per-user bandwidth figure; targets mixnets whose nodes fail or drop packets (active-attack surface).

title: Security Analysis of Signal's PQXDH Handshake
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Game-based reductionist security analysis of Signal's PQXDH in a maximum-exposure model (fine-grained compromise of long-term, semi-static and ephemeral keys against classical and quantum adversaries), capturing the KEM component and the signing of public keys; establishes concrete security bounds for PQXDH.

title: A Deniability Analysis of Signal's Initial Handshake PQXDH
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Shows PQXDH does not meet X3DH's deniability because of the signature on the ephemeral key; analysis relies on plaintext awareness of the KEM, which Signal's PQXDH implementation does not provide; initiator and responder get different deniability guarantees due to protocol asymmetry; introduces a finer-grained deniability model (including malicious adversaries in the big-brother model).

title: Effective Anonymous Messaging: the Role of Altruism
bitmessage_link: Game-theoretic model of FMD: users choose how much cover traffic to download; selfish users do not, so anonymity needs altruists; the incentive version of the Bitmessage bandwidth cost.
note: Preprint.

title: Careless Whisper: Exploiting Silent Delivery Receipts to Monitor Users on Mobile Instant Messengers
