bitmessage_link: Delivery receipts are a metadata channel absent in Bitmessage (no ACKs), but trade off reliability.
note: Silent delivery receipts triggered by crafted messages let any user who knows a phone number ping the target without notification, in WhatsApp and Signal: tracks the target across companion devices, infers daily schedule and activity, counts active sessions and OS, and drains battery or data. A metadata leak by design of receipts, independent of E2EE.

title: Weak Consistency mode in Key Transparency: OPTIKS
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Adds an auditor-free mode to OPTIKS key transparency with slightly weaker security (weak consistency), formalised and proved.

title: Onion Franking: Abuse Reports for Mix-Based Private Messaging
bitmessage_link: Abuse reporting for mix-based systems; handles the spam/abuse problem that Bitmessage handled only with proof-of-work.
note: Cost model: abuse-reporting mechanisms for any onion-encrypted private messaging system, including low-latency opportunistic mixing and mixnets; claims lower overhead than prior metadata-hiding abuse reporting and stronger threat models; see paper for numbers.

title: Obfuscated Key Exchange
bitmessage_link: Handshake indistinguishability for transport under a global observer; pairs with ciphertext key-privacy.
note: Formalizes obfuscated key exchange and obfuscated KEMs (OKEMs) and proposes pq-obfs, a post-quantum drop-in for Tor's obfs4 using ML-KEM encodings.

title: OCash: Fully Anonymous Payments between Blockchain Light Clients
bitmessage_link: Position-hint approach to finding your messages: the recipient fetches a few candidate slots instead of trial-decrypting everything, with the slot choice hidden from the serving node.
note: Anonymous payments where the light client stays private even from the full nodes it reads through: a tree-ORAM variant shuffles payments on-chain while telling the client a few positions among which to find its payment, so it never scans the chain nor reveals which entries it reads. UC-proved; introduces anonymous-coin-friendly encryption and compressible randomness beacons. No concrete cost figure recorded here.

title: A message broker architecture for adaptive data exchange in the IoT
note: Abstract not retrieved; included on title and venue (21st IEEE International Conference on Software Architecture (ICSA)).

title: Deanonymizing Ethereum Validators: The P2P Network Has a Privacy Issue
note: Shows validators can be mapped to IP addresses by observing attestation propagation in GossipSub subnets (15% of validators).

title: Mixnet Research Review
bitmessage_link: Literature overview from a deployed-mixnet team: topology, compromising latency versus bandwidth, evolution since Chaum.
note: Cost model: survey of designs; no new measurements.

title: PIR with Client-Side Preprocessing: Information-Theoretic Constructions and Lower Bounds
bitmessage_link: Mailbox/board systems that replace Bitmessage's flood with indexed or oblivious retrieval; they hide the recipient from the storage nodes but need a rendezvous or shared-secret schedule that Bitmessage addresses do not give.
note: First study of information-theoretic single-server PIR with client preprocessing: new constructions with trade-offs between server computation, client space and bandwidth, a near-tight client-space versus bandwidth lower bound, and a result that beating it with a natural syntactic computational scheme would imply a hard problem in SZK.

title: DPPS: A Decentralised Publish-Process-Subscribe Middleware with Verifiable Computations
note: Abstract not retrieved; classified from the title as core work on pub/sub.

title: ZK-DPPS: A Zero-Knowledge Decentralised Data Sharing and Processing Middleware
note: Zero-knowledge decentralised data sharing and processing middleware, a successor to DPPS.

title: Symmetric Signcryption and E2EE Group Messaging in Keybase
bitmessage_link: Chan-style shared-key groups with sender signatures are exactly this primitive (Bitmessage signs objects).
note: Introduces symmetric signcryption (sender and recipient share a secret key) and proves that composing symmetric encryption and signatures achieves strong security against attackers learning and controlling many keys; models the core Keybase encrypted group messaging algorithm as symmetric signcryption and proves it secure under non-standard, brittle assumptions on the primitives; the model later used for MLS, Session

title: HomeRun: High-efficiency Oblivious Message Retrieval, Unrestricted
bitmessage_link: OMR variant without a bound on pending messages.
note: Cost model: see paper.

title: Benchmarking post-quantum cryptography in Ethereum-based blockchains
bitmessage_link: Replication multiplies per-object size, as in a flooded network.
note: Benchmarks ECDSA against Dilithium, Falcon-1024 and SPHINCS+ on real-time Ethereum transaction data (transaction signatures only, not BLS consensus signatures). Dilithium2 verification is more than 4x faster than ECDSA (Dilithium5 2.1x) and its summed time and memory is only about 12% and 20% above ECDSA; Falcon-1024 signing takes about 224x and simplest-mode SPHINCS+ signing about 2057x ECDSA time. Signature and key

title: Bluesky and the AT Protocol: Usable Decentralized Social Media
note: Describes the AT Protocol: per-user repositories, relays that aggregate the firehose, and app views.

title: EROR: Efficient Repliable Onion Routing with Strong Provable Privacy
bitmessage_link: Reply-capable onion packet format with hop-by-hop integrity, preventing tagging attacks that threaten both Sphinx and Bitmessage-like static-key designs.
note: Cost model: efficient packet format with integrity protection; compared with other repliable onion schemes (heavier SNARG-based option).

title: Privacy Comparison for Bitcoin Light Client Implementations
bitmessage_link: Measured privacy/bandwidth trade-off of the two deployed ways to avoid downloading everything: server-side Bloom filter versus client-side filtering.
note: Defines privacy metrics and compares SPV (BIP 37 Bloom filters) with Neutrino (BIP 157/158 filters) on real Bitcoin data over time, showing the privacy-versus-communication trade-off; proposes general privacy-enhancing techniques and an SPV 'aggregation model' with better privacy.

title: DISC-NG: Robust Service Discovery in the Ethereum Global Network
note: DISC-NG: Robust Service Discovery in the Ethereum Global Network.

title: Single Pass Client-Preprocessing Private Information Retrieval
bitmessage_link: Replaces broadcast-and-trial-decrypt with indexed private retrieval: the recipient fetches only its slots and the server learns nothing about which; works only if the recipient can compute or look up the slot (a rendezvous or mailbox index)
note: Client-preprocessing PIR whose offline phase is exactly one linear pass over the database, concretely optimal for preprocessing; no per-client server storage.

title: SophOMR: Improved Oblivious Message Retrieval from SIMD-Aware Homomorphic Compression
bitmessage_link: Removes the need for every recipient to download and trial-decrypt the whole board, which is Bitmessage's recipient-ambiguity mechanism, while keeping the server blind to who each message is for; stronger than a fuzzy filter but needs FHE o
note: New homomorphic compression using the SIMD structure of the HE scheme. Versus PerfOMR for 65,536 payloads of 612 bytes with up to 50 pertinent: 3.4x lower runtime, 2.2x smaller digest, 1.5x smaller key; the compression step alone is 7.5x faster.

title: ELEKTRA: Efficient Lightweight multi-dEvice Key TRAnsparency
bitmessage_link: Multi-device key management for the directory, the device-level counterpart of Sesame's session management.
note: Formalises the Multi-Device Verifiable Key Directory (MVKD) with completeness, extraction-based soundness and privacy, and gives ELEKTRA, combining the Keybase KT core with identity-key management across a user's devices so that devices can help monitor and prevent fake-key registration.

title: A Formal Analysis of Apple's iMessage PQ3 Protocol
bitmessage_link: Second deployed example of amortising post-quantum key material in a messenger.
note: Tamarin analysis of Apple PQ3: ECDH ratcheting plus periodic ML-KEM rekeying (ML-KEM-768 for ephemeral KEM keys, ML-KEM-1024 for prekeys, 1568 B key and ciphertext). Establishes forward secrecy and post-compromise security including post-quantum, with caveats on authentication.

title: A Formal Analysis of Apple’s iMessage PQ3 Protocol
bitmessage_link: Gives a verified reference point for post-quantum session security in a production messenger.
note: Formal verification (Tamarin) of Apple's iMessage PQ3: hybrid post-quantum initialisation then Signal-like ratchet with PQ rekeying; proves confidentiality, authentication, forward secrecy and post-compromise security (including post-quantum PCS) for the specified fine-grained compromise scenarios, and extracts the exact conditions and caveats (such as rekeying conditions) for PQ-PCS.

title: PerfOMR: Oblivious Message Retrieval with Reduced Communication and Computation
bitmessage_link: OMR improvement with lower communication and computation.
note: Cost model: see paper; reduces digest size and server cost versus the CRYPTO 2022 OMR.

title: Snake-eye Resistant PKE from LWE for Oblivious Message Retrieval and Robust Encryption
bitmessage_link: Spam by malicious senders is Bitmessage's reason for proof-of-work; here it is a cryptographic property.
note: Proves OMRp2 DoS-resistant under LWE, shows PerfOMR-style schemes are attackable by malicious senders, and builds LWEmongrass (snake-eye resistant PKE, hence robust PKE); DoS-PerfOMR is 12x faster than OMRp2.

title: The Matrix Reloaded: A Mechanized Formal Analysis of the Matrix Cryptographic Suite
bitmessage_link: Mechanised-proof baseline for deployed group messaging; no counterpart exists for Bitmessage.
note: ProVerif symbolic models of Olm, Megolm and their composition (and of Sender Keys and Signal+Sender Keys): proves authentication, confidentiality, forward secrecy and PCS where they hold and mechanises known limitations and attacks. Content/session security only.

title: Security of Symmetric Ratchets and Key Chains - Implications for Protocols like TLS 1.3, Signal, and PQ3
bitmessage_link: Relevant to any design that derives per-message keys by hashing a chain; chain length and skipped keys are exposed in store-and-forward delivery.
note: Analyses one-way key chains and symmetric ratchets (TLS 1.3, Signal, MLS, PQ3): the hash-chain construction used by Signal and PQ3 has weak keys and an unexpectedly high rate of key collisions after many steps (security degrades with chain length), while other constructions do not; recommends constructions and chain-length limits.

title: Runtime Verification Containers for Publish/Subscribe Networks
note: Publish/subscribe (pub/sub) networks are a cornerstone of modern distributed systems, playing a crucial role in applications like the Internet of Things (IoT) and robotics.

title: YPIR: High-Throughput Single-Server PIR with Silent Preprocessing
bitmessage_link: PIR with no client-side hint, useful when messaging clients are stateless.
note: Cost model: 12.1 GB/s/core and 2.5 MB total communication for a 32 GB database with no offline communication.

title: Midnight ledger specification: Zswap (shielded coin protocol)
bitmessage_link: Same structure as Bitmessage for recipient discovery: outputs are public and recipients must scan; no tags.
note: Zswap: commitment/nullifier sets for shielded coins; output carries an optional ciphertext (DH over embedded curve, Poseidon-CTR) delivering the coin secret to the receiver. Hides amount, owner and sender-receiver link; the spec defines no messaging channel or event type, and ciphertext presence is optional (delivery may go offchain).

title: Towards Self-Optimization of Publish/Subscribe IoT Systems using Continuous Performance Monitoring
note: This paper proposes in this paper a continuous performance monitoring methodology, applied on IoT systems based on Publish/subscribe communication model, that relies on a Stochastic Petri nets modelling and analysis to assess performances.

title: Stealth and Beyond: Attribute-Driven Accountability in Bitcoin Transactions
bitmessage_link: Shows stealth recipient keys can carry attributes; relevant to proving rights to a recipient tag without revealing the address.
note: Identity-Based Matchmaking Stealth Signatures: stealth addresses carrying compliance attributes so both sender and recipient satisfy policy, compatible with Bitcoin as is.

title: AUPE: Collaborative byzantine fault-tolerant peer-sampling
note: Collaborative Byzantine fault-tolerant peer sampling.

title: FIPS 203: Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (ML-KEM)
bitmessage_link: Ciphertext and key sizes matter for Bitmessage-style flooding where every object is replicated to every node.
note: Standardises ML-KEM-512/768/1024 (IND-CCA2 KEM from module-LWE); the post-quantum KEM used in PQXDH, SPQR, PQ3, X-Wing and MLS PQ ciphersuites; no sender authentication, and encapsulation keys are about 800-1568 bytes.

title: FIPS 204: Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA)
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage signs every object with ECDSA and carries the sender key in the object; ML-DSA signatures are tens of times larger than ECDSA signatures.
note: Standardises ML-DSA-44/65/87 (Fiat-Shamir with aborts over module lattices), the main post-quantum signature candidate for messaging identity keys and MLS credentials; signatures are about 2.4-4.6 kB and public keys 1.3-2.6 kB, much larger than Ed25519.

title: FIPS 205: Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard (SLH-DSA)
bitmessage_link: Signature size is prohibitive for per-object signing in a flooded network.
note: Standardises SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+), a hash-based stateless signature with conservative assumptions but 8-50 kB signatures; the fallback to lattice assumptions for long-lived identity or root keys.

title: NIST IR 8547 (initial public draft): Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
bitmessage_link: Policy clock against which a successor's long-term confidentiality target is set.
note: Proposes deprecating 112-bit-strength quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms after 2030 and disallowing all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms (128-bit and above) after 2035; frames the harvest-now-decrypt-later risk for long-lived confidentiality.

title: MixMatch: Flow Matching for Mixnet Traffic
bitmessage_link: Measures how well a passive adversary at the edges can match flows through Nym; cover traffic reduces but does not remove flow correlation.
note: Cost model: empirical attack on the Nym design with three classifiers (statistical and deep learning); real traffic datasets released. Tests Loopix-derived packet schedule with cover traffic against a passive observer.

title: Decentralized Information-Flow Control for ROS2
note: We present Picaros, a DIFC system tailored for ROS2.

title: ADPS: Providing asynchronous PubSub communication in an adaptive and scalable way in Edge-Fog-Cloud architectures for healthcare data traffic
note: This document introduces ADPS (Asynchronous Distributed Publish Subscribe), a PubSub-based communication model tailored for a hierarchical architecture distributed on Edge, Fog, and Cloud layers.

title: LARMix: Latency-Aware Routing in Mix Networks
bitmessage_link: Cuts mixnet latency without a full anonymity penalty; shows the trilemma tuning that lets a low-latency mixnet replace Bitmessage's hours-long flooding.
note: Cost model: propagation latency reduced as much as 8x (120 ms to 15 ms) with about 2 bits entropy loss; load balancing 3.5x latency cut while less than halving the anonymity set.

title: LARMix++: Latency-Aware Routing in Mix Networks with Free Routes Topology
bitmessage_link: Extension of LARMix to free-route (non-stratified) mixnets.
note: Cost model: latency-aware routing for free-route topologies; see LARMix for headline numbers.

title: Message Latency in Waku Relay with Rate Limiting Nullifiers
note: Analytic model, 1000-node simulation and 5-site deployment of Waku Relay (GossipSub + RLN) latency.

title: RFC 9576: The Privacy Pass Architecture
bitmessage_link: Standard framework for admission tokens that carry no identity.
note: Architecture of Privacy Pass with Client, Attester, Issuer and Origin and deployment models (same-party and split) and privacy considerations (issuer view, collusion, token-count side channels). Adversary: colluding issuer, attester and origin who link users through timing, token metadata or anonymity-set size.

title: RFC 9577: The Privacy Pass HTTP Authentication Scheme
bitmessage_link: Wire format for anonymous tokens; applicable to relay admission.
note: HTTP authentication scheme and token challenge format for Privacy Pass. Adversary: origin that tries to link tokens across redemptions via challenge reuse or per-origin binding.

title: RFC 9578: Privacy Pass Issuance Protocols
bitmessage_link: Concrete token types for stamps.
note: Two issuance protocols: privately verifiable (VOPRF) and publicly verifiable (blind RSA). Adversary: malicious issuer attempting key-based tagging attacks; attacker replaying tokens.

title: Outfox: a Postquantum Packet Format for Layered Mixnets
bitmessage_link: Sphinx-like format for fixed-length stratified routes with KEM-based per-hop keys and a UC security proof; the Nym packet format roadmap.
note: Cost model: removes a full key exchange and uses compact per-hop headers, lowering computation and communication versus KEM-Sphinx. Applies to constant-length routes such as Loopix.

title: ZIPNet: Low-bandwidth anonymous broadcast from (dis)Trusted Execution Environments
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.
note: Cost model: DC-net-like anonymous vector scheme; 4.2x to 7.6x lower server runtime than the state of the art; outsources almost all server inbound traffic and about 80 percent of computation to aggregators that are untrusted for anonymity; scales to hundreds of any-trust servers (trust diversity). Trust: anytrust servers (as Dissent) for privacy; client-side TEEs used only for DoS prevention, not for privacy, so a br

title: Provable Security for the Onion Routing and Mix Network Packet Format Sphinx
bitmessage_link: First detailed security proof of Sphinx; shows DDH is not enough (Gap-DH needed) and finds a sender-privacy attack on the integrated-system service model.
note: Cost model: no system numbers; adaptation embeds reply information in the payload and removes the nymserver at modest cost.

title: Session network documentation: Onion requests and message routing; Swarms
bitmessage_link: Swarm-addressed delivery trades Bitmessage's whole-network recipient ambiguity for a small, public set of nodes per recipient, plus onion hops for sender anonymity.
note: Sender fetches the recipient's swarm mapping by Account ID, then sends the message through a 3-hop onion request to a random swarm node, which replicates it to the swarm; stored until expiry (two weeks default). Hides sender IP from the swarm; the swarm for an Account ID is public, so who is receiving (and the volume and timing) is visible to its swarm nodes. Onion requests are TCP-based and limited to small messages

title: Privacy-Preserving Contact Tracing System based on a Publish-Subscribe Model
note: This paper introduces a technique for enhancing Privacy in contact-tracing systems while preserving the data for research purposes.

title: Post-quantum resistant augmented double ratchet algorithm (PQDR)
bitmessage_link: Direct answer to Bitmessage's lack of any ratchet; adds PQ-hybrid session security to a metadata-private queue system.
note: Augments Signal double ratchet with encrypted headers and a hybrid Curve448+sntrup761 KEM in each ratchet step; compares with Signal PQXDH and Tutanota hybrid approaches. Content-only property (PQ forward secrecy and PCS); metadata unaffected.

title: Cryptographic Analysis of Delta Chat
bitmessage_link: Shows weakness of email-based group E2EE without ratchets; no forward secrecy, like Bitmessage.
note: Attacks on Delta Chat's Autocrypt/SecureJoin/OpenPGP use: key-confusion, group membership and signature issues; Delta Chat inherits email-server metadata exposure. Analysis is of content authentication and group security, not metadata.

title: Security analysis of the iMessage PQ3 protocol
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Computational-model security analysis of PQ3: shows classical and post-quantum confidentiality with forward secrecy and post-compromise secrecy under reductions to underlying primitives; authentication remains classical.

title: Distributed PIR: Scaling Private Messaging via the Users' Machines
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.
note: Cost model: shifts most PIR computation to users' machines, 3.25x and 4.31x improvement over prior PIR-based messaging systems with the gap widening as users grow. Trust: no honest server required for privacy.

title: SimpleX Chat Design Review: summary report (Trail of Bits, 2024-08-12)
bitmessage_link: Reviews the PQ ratchet and 2-hop routing that supersede Bitmessage-style static-key and flooding designs.
note: Design review of SMP, private routing and XRCP: protocols are only informally specified; a user-correlating side channel via the GET command; a compromised transport protocol enables more efficient correlation attacks; user correlation by introduced latency; XRCP lacks PFS and break-in recovery within sessions. Metadata-relevant findings about correlating users across queues.

title: To Squelch or not to Squelch: Enabling Improved Message Dissemination on the XRP Ledger
note: Evaluates XRPL's squelching mechanism for reducing redundant message dissemination; companion to the GossipSub-on-XRPL line.

title: ADVERSARIAL-MODELS: Waku v2 adversarial models and attack-based threat list
bitmessage_link: Threat list for Waku relay, filter, store and lightpush: sybil, eclipse, DoS, deanonymisation by the filter/store node.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: GOSSIPSUB-TOR-PUSH
bitmessage_link: Publishes the first hop of a message through Tor to hide the origin IP from relay peers; a source-anonymity patch for gossip networks.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: LIBP2P-MIX (mix protocol for libp2p)
bitmessage_link: Sphinx-based mix layer for libp2p and Waku with cover traffic and DoS protection; replaces flooding by routed mix paths for sender anonymity.
note: Living spec, large; also relevant to mixnet slices.

title: NOISE-X3DH-DOUBLE-RATCHET
bitmessage_link: Noise-based session establishment plus double ratchet for Waku chat; the post-compromise security layer missing from Bitmessage.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: RLN-STEALTH-COMMITMENTS
bitmessage_link: Stealth-address-like commitments so RLN membership registrations are unlinkable to the registrant.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: RLN-V2 (Rate Limit Nullifier V2)
bitmessage_link: RLN with a per-epoch message budget instead of one message per epoch.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: An Empirical Analysis of the Nostr Social Network: Decentralization, Availability, and Replication Overhead
bitmessage_link: Measures relay availability, concentration and replication overhead; context for the cost and reliability of relay-based delivery that NIP-17 inherits.
note: Not about DMs specifically.

title: XIP-46: Multi-wallet identity
bitmessage_link: Wallet identity makes the social graph linkable by chain address; contrast with Bitmessage's pseudonymous addresses.
note: Replaces wallet-address identity with Inbox IDs bound to multiple wallets and installations. Associations are public to the network: wallet-to-inbox links are not hidden.

title: XIP-49: Decentralized backend for MLS messages
bitmessage_link: MLS group security over a permissioned, paid broker mesh with on-chain ordering of identity/membership; opposite end of the spectrum from Bitmessage's anonymous flood.
note: Architecture for a decentralised XMTP: node-to-node and client-to-node protocols, permissioned node registry as NFTs, identity updates ordered on a blockchain, payers compensating node operators. Clients provide MLS E2EE; nodes see wallet-linked inbox IDs, group membership events, message sizes and timing. Hides only content.

title: Unconditional Security using (Random) Anonymous Bulletin Board
bitmessage_link: What can be built on top of an anonymous bulletin board such as a Bitmessage stream.
note: Key agreement and string OT in the anonymous bulletin board model (Ishai et al. FOCS 2006): 200% throughput improvement for key agreement with a near-optimality proof, 1-round chosen-message random string OT, and a 1-round lower bound for BEC under stated conditions.

title: Honeybee: Byzantine Tolerant Decentralized Peer Sampling with Verifiable Random Walks
note: Byzantine-tolerant peer sampling; includes a simulation of GossipSub peer discovery with peer exchange.

title: Examining I2P Resilience: Effect of Centrality-based Attack
bitmessage_link: Availability limits of an anonymity network transport.
note: Models I2P as a graph and evaluates removal of high-centrality routers. Adversary: attacker capable of removing or degrading the most central routers.

title: The Best of Both KEMs: Securely Combining KEMs in Post-quantum Hybrid Schemes
bitmessage_link: Directly reduces the per-hop or per-message size cost of hybrid post-quantum encryption.
note: Generalises X-Wing: when combining several KEMs, one may omit the ciphertext of any KEM with ciphertext second-preimage resistance (C2PRI) provided the key combiner is a split-key PRF. Saves up to a full component ciphertext (1088 B for ML-KEM-768) per hybrid encapsulation.

title: Recommendations for Key-Encapsulation Mechanisms (NIST SP 800-227)
bitmessage_link: Reference rules for upgrading a classical ECDH step to a hybrid KEM combiner.
note: NIST guidance on using KEMs (including ML-KEM): security properties (IND-CCA), key-derivation and combiner requirements, and rules for hybrid constructions mixing classical and post-quantum shared secrets.

title: Formal Analysis of Multi-Device Group Messaging in WhatsApp
bitmessage_link: Gives the precise formal guarantees of the largest group-messaging deployment, none of which exist for Bitmessage chans.
note: Formal description of WhatsApp's multi-device group messaging (from public documentation plus reverse engineering) in an extended Device-Oriented Group Messaging model with device revocation; states and proves the security guarantees it provides and discusses limitations of those guarantees.

title: Continuous Group-Key Agreement: Concurrent Updates without Pruning
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: CGKA with concurrent updates but without pruning (not discarding concurrent updates); retains PCS with logarithmic cost.

title: How to Compare Bandwidth Constrained Two-Party Secure Messaging Protocols: A Quest for A More Efficient and Secure Post-Quantum Protocol
bitmessage_link: Makes the bandwidth-versus-healing trade-off explicit, central for any flooded network.
note: Proposes a pragmatic metric of how secure a messaging protocol is given a particular communication pattern, to compare bandwidth-constrained post-quantum protocols (PQ3, Triple Ratchet and new designs); shows there is no 'optimal' protocol since designs are incomparable under worst-case adversarial messaging behaviour with real bandwidth limits; develops a framework and a more efficient and secure PQ protocol.

title: Post Quantum Migration of Tor
bitmessage_link: Best single costing of post-quantum primitives inside an anonymity network; sizes translate to per-message cost in a flooding successor.
note: Inventories Tor's primitives and estimates the cost of replacing them. Key sizes in bytes: ML-KEM encapsulation key/decapsulation key/ciphertext as in FIPS 203, HQC-128/192/256 encapsulation key 2249/4522/7245; ML-DSA key plus signature 3732 B; Tor CREATE handshake limit 505 B versus 693 B for ntruees443ep1; only ML-KEM-512/768 and sntrup761 (KEMs) and Falcon-512 and ML-DSA-44 (signatures) are judged viable. Estimate

title: The Messaging Layer Security (MLS) Architecture
bitmessage_link: Names the metadata a delivery service sees in a modern group messenger; a useful baseline for what flooding-based designs can improve.
note: Describes the delivery service and authentication service roles around MLS and the security model; states what MLS does not hide (group size, membership, sender identity metadata to the delivery service, message timing) and the trust assumptions on the authentication service.

title: bitchat Protocol Whitepaper (version 2.0, July 2026)
bitmessage_link: BLE mesh with controlled flood, TTL, dedup and jitter, Noise-encrypted private messages, Nostr bridge; states that unlinkable presence is not provided and packet length is observable. A flood-based relative of Bitmessage at the radio layer.
note: Version 2.0 dated 2026-07-06; first release 2025. Author attribution to the project, not a named person.

title: Source-Based Routing for BitChat Packets (v2)
bitmessage_link: Replaces flooding with explicit source routes for known peers to cut radio load.
note: Project doc; undated beyond repository history.

title: A Note on Notes: Towards Scalable Anonymous Payments via Evolving Nullifiers and Oblivious Synchronization
bitmessage_link: Same delegation idea (an untrusted server does the heavy per-ledger work for a client without learning its transactions) applied to coin-state proofs instead of message detection.
note: Oblivious synchronization: a user asks an untrusted remote service that ingests the public ledger for succinct proofs that its coins are unspent and valid; the service is oblivious to the client's transactions, keeps only ephemeral per-client state, and clients can switch services. Primarily about pruning the ever-growing nullifier set, not note discovery; included as the Zcash designers' model for outsourcing wallet

title: Everlasting Anonymous Rate-Limited Tokens
bitmessage_link: Separates long-term privacy from short-term unforgeability: exactly the asymmetry an admission check on a flooded network needs.
note: Anonymous rate-limited tokens whose anonymity survives later quantum attack on stored tokens (everlasting privacy) while unforgeability may rely on classical assumptions; dispenser yields up to k unlinkable tokens. Explicit answer to record-now-decrypt-later for token metadata.

title: OnionPIRv2: Efficient Single-Server PIR
bitmessage_link: Replaces broadcast-and-trial-decrypt with indexed private retrieval: the recipient fetches only its slots and the server learns nothing about which; works only if the recipient can compute or look up the slot (a rendezvous or mailbox index)
note: Engineering update of OnionPIR: 3.7x response overhead for 3 KB entries and up to 1372 MB/s server throughput.

title: Private Signaling Secure Against Actively Corrupted Servers
bitmessage_link: Same board-plus-signal model as Bitmessage's flooded object pool, with an outsourced detection step so recipients no longer scan everything; trust moves to a TEE or to non-colluding servers.
note: TEE-free private signaling with two non-colluding servers, either of which may be actively corrupted; retrieval is cast as a PSI-like problem with custom ZK proofs for consistency with the board. Digest 33.57 KB for a board of 2^19 messages; retrieving signals takes about 2 minutes on 16 threads over a LAN.

title: GURKE: Group Unidirectional Ratcheted Key Exchange
bitmessage_link: One-to-many ratcheting matches the Bitmessage broadcast/subscription pattern, where one sender writes to many readers.
note: Group unidirectional ratcheted key exchange: restricts CGKA so that members are either senders or receivers (a sender group Alice establishes keys to a receiver group Bob), giving forward security and post-compromise security for the sender side and forward security for receivers, with constructions simpler and cheaper than full CGKA.

title: Towards Leakage-Resilient Ratcheted Key Exchange
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Formalises a key-indistinguishability game for unidirectional ratcheted key exchange (one sender, one receiver) with partial leakage of party state rather than only full state exposure, building on Balli-Rosler-Vaudenay, with constructions that keep forward security and post-compromise security under bounded leakage.

title: Signal Protocol and Post-Quantum Ratchets
bitmessage_link: Deployment account of post-quantum session security at scale; contrast with Bitmessage's single static key per address.
note: Announces the Sparse Post-Quantum Ratchet and explains the design: ML-KEM ratchet state machine, key/ciphertext chunking, mixed into the classical ratchet; goals are forward secrecy and post-compromise security against quantum adversaries, with hybrid security (secure if either ratchet holds).

title: Performance Evaluation of Brokerless Messaging Libraries
note: Messaging systems are essential for efficiently transferring large volumes of data, ensuring rapid response times and high-throughput communication.

title: ETK: External-Operations TreeKEM and the Security of MLS in RFC 9420
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Security proof for RFC 9420 TreeKEM including external operations (external commits and proposals) that earlier analyses of drafts omitted; ETK (External-Operations TreeKEM) models these and shows the final standard meets its goals, with some corrections.

title: sPAR: (Somewhat) Practical Anonymous Router
bitmessage_link: Anonymous router with cryptographic anonymity using lightweight primitives.
note: Cost model: practical construction of the Shi-Wu non-interactive anonymous router, where a single untrusted server permutes a set of messages without learning the permutation; aims to remove the need for any honest router and to fix the theory-only constructions. See paper for per-user costs. Trust: one untrusted server (cryptographic anonymity).

title: Causal Analysis of GossipSub Mesh Parameters Over the XRP Ledger
note: Causal analysis of GossipSub mesh degree parameters on XRPL traffic.

title: KATT Efficient publish subscribe telemetry transport in a hierarchical Kademlia topology
note: Traditional Internet of things systems suffer from limitations inherent to the clientserver architecture, with the entire system being dependant on the correct functionality of the server.

title: Triple Ratchet: A Bandwidth Efficient Hybrid-Secure Signal Protocol
bitmessage_link: Shows bandwidth cost for PQ continuous key agreement, relevant where each message must be flooded.
note: Hybrid classical/PQ ratchet that adds a sparse KEM-based ratchet to the Signal double ratchet, cutting the bandwidth of PQ updates; the basis of Signal's deployed SPQR. Content/session security only.

title: Anonymous Rate-Limited Credentials (draft-yun-cfrg-arc-01)
bitmessage_link: Standards-track form of the anonymous rate limit that RLN provides on-chain; direct replacement for per-object proof of work.
note: Keyed-verification anonymous credential that can be presented up to a fixed number of times per context, each presentation bound to client secrets and public application context and unlinkable to other presentations. Adversary: client trying to exceed its presentation limit or link/forge; issuer-verifier trying to link presentations.

title: The BBS Signature Scheme (draft-irtf-cfrg-bbs-signatures-12)
bitmessage_link: Primitive for unlinkable multi-show credentials, e.g. membership or reputation proofs without identity.
note: Specification of BBS signatures with multi-message signing and unlinkable zero-knowledge proofs of knowledge supporting selective disclosure. Adversary: forger under q-type assumption in pairing groups; verifier attempting to link proofs.

title: X-Wing: general-purpose hybrid post-quantum KEM (Internet-Draft)
bitmessage_link: Implementable spec for the hybrid KEM that Outfox and Katzenpost instantiate.
note: Specification of X-Wing: 32-byte secret key seed, 1216-byte encapsulation key (1184 ML-KEM + 32 X25519), 1120-byte ciphertext (1088 + 32), 32-byte shared secret; KEM combiner SHA3-256(ss_M || ss_X || ct_X || pk_X || label).

title: Technical Note: LeanSig for Post-Quantum Ethereum
bitmessage_link: Design for post-quantum signatures in a gossip network where every node relays every signature.
note: XMSS-variant hash-based multi-signature family tuned for aggregation in Ethereum consensus gossip, trading signature size against verification hashing via an incomparable encoding; stateful hash signatures keep keys and signatures small enough for gossip when aggregated.

title: Terminology for Post-Quantum Traditional Hybrid Schemes
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Defines PQ/T hybrid terminology (PQ/T hybrid key establishment, composite, non-composite, hybrid signature); no security claims, but fixes vocabulary used by hybrid-KEM and hybrid-signature work in messaging.

title: PREAMBLE and IMRECEIVING for Improved Large Message Handling in libp2p GossipSub
note: Control-message extensions (PREAMBLE, IMRECEIVING) to avoid duplicate large-message transfers in GossipSub.

title: Staggering and Fragmentation for Improved Large Message Handling in libp2p GossipSub
note: Staggered sending and message fragmentation to cut GossipSub latency and bandwidth for large messages.

title: Reliable Image Transmission in CPS-based Pub/Sub
note: Developments in communication and automation have driven the expansion of distributed networks, essential for IoT and CPS development in industrial applications requiring reliable image processing and real-time adaptability.

title: Shadowfax: Hybrid Security and Deniability for AKEMs
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Shadowfax: hybrid-secure authenticated KEM that combines a classical non-interactive key exchange, a post-quantum KEM and a post-quantum ring signature to preserve deniability (which X3DH has but PQXDH and PQ3 lose) while keeping hybrid confidentiality; deniability in both dishonest and honest settings.

title: How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits
bitmessage_link: Shrinks the horizon for recorded Bitmessage ciphertexts.
note: Lowers the estimate to fewer than one million noisy physical qubits and under a week of runtime for RSA-2048 (approximate-residue arithmetic, yoked surface codes, magic-state cultivation), roughly a 20x reduction in qubits relative to 2019.

title: Crypto Wars in Secure Messaging: Covert Channels in Signal Despite Leaked Keys
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Anamorphic constructions embedding covert messages in the existing Signal Double Ratchet (in the DH keys of the asymmetric ratchet or in symmetric-ratchet authentication tags), letting users communicate covertly even against an adversary that can decrypt all Signal traffic (mandated access or leaked keys).

title: Multi-server Fuzzy Message Detection
bitmessage_link: Attacks Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt directly: the recipient hands a detection key to an untrusted node that filters the board, so the client downloads roughly a fraction p of traffic instead of everything, at the price of an anonym
note: Extends FMD to several servers holding different detection keys extracted from one secret key, so the receiver combines their results locally: servers can use high false-positive rates (more privacy) while the combined rate seen by the receiver stays low (less bandwidth). Formalises stealth public keys for FMD and gives two constructions, one with short public keys. No benchmark numbers in the abstract.

title: Hybrid Obfuscated Key Exchange and KEMs
bitmessage_link: Random-looking post-quantum ciphertexts are the precondition for recipient-anonymous flooding and for censorship-resistant transport.
note: First OKEM combiner with hybrid IND-CCA security and hybrid ciphertext-obfuscation guarantees (public keys and ciphertexts that look like random bitstrings), used to build Drivel, a pq-obfs variant for hybrid obfs4. Plain hybrid KEM combiners do not give hybrid obfuscation. Builds on Kemeleon, which encodes ML-KEM keys and ciphertexts as random-looking strings under decision module-LWE (not statistically indistinguis

title: Practical Keyword Private Information Retrieval from Key-to-Index Mappings
bitmessage_link: Faster tag lookups for topic-addressed boards.
note: Reduces keyword PIR to index PIR through compact key-to-index mappings; 15x-178x less communication and 1.1x-2.4x faster than ChalametPIR; 47 ms for 1 million 32-byte entries.

title: Bundled Authenticated Key Exchange: A Concrete Treatment of (Post-Quantum) Signal's Handshake Protocol
bitmessage_link: Static-key encryption is Bitmessage's weakness; this is the formal treatment of the asynchronous handshake that fixes it, post-quantum.
note: Unified model for prekey-bundle handshakes; shows X3DH and PQXDH (harvest-now-decrypt-later secure, not fully post-quantum authenticated) fall short of optimal security and proposes RingXKEM, a fully post-quantum handshake sharing state across prekey bundles, with a size and efficiency comparison.

title: Exploring How to Authenticate Application Messages in MLS: More Efficient, Post-Quantum, and Anonymous Blocklistable
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage signs every object; this line trades signatures against deniability and size.
note: Authentication of MLS application messages: replaces per-message EdDSA with more efficient, post-quantum and anonymously blocklistable alternatives; shows trade-offs between non-repudiation and deniability within groups.

title: Hamming Quasi-Cyclic (HQC): specification, 22 August 2025
bitmessage_link: Different hardness assumption to lattices at 4-14 KB per ciphertext.
note: Sizes in bytes (encapsulation key / decapsulation key / ciphertext / shared key): HQC-1 2241/2321/4433/32, HQC-3 4514/4602/8978/32, HQC-5 7237/7333/14421/32. Security: quasi-cyclic syndrome decoding; Xagawa found anonymity fails for two of three early parameter sets.

title: Echomix: a Strong Anonymity System with Messaging
bitmessage_link: Describes Katzenpost as a Loopix-descendant with PQ Sphinx, a group messaging protocol (BACAP and Pigeonhole) and store-and-retrieve for offline users; closest modern analogue of Bitmessage's object pool with metadata privacy.
note: Cost model: Poisson-delayed mix layers, decoy loops, hybrid PQ nested packet encryption; the paper gives latency and bandwidth overhead evaluations. Trust: global adversary, compromised contacts and infrastructure, quantum adversaries; second-party (contact) adversary minimised.

title: Analyzing Group Chat Encryption in MLS, Session, Signal, and Matrix
bitmessage_link: Session is the Bitmessage-lineage messenger; the paper shows its group encryption has the same signature-binding weakness as peers.
note: Analyses the composition of symmetric encryption and signatures in the chat layers of MLS, Session, Signal and Matrix (symmetric signcryption formalism): practically exploitable replay and reordering attacks by a group insider in MLS and Session; a forgery attack by an outsider holding a user's signing key in Signal (previously found by Balbas et al.); Matrix is saved by ecosystem mitigations; gives security theorems

title: Navigating Decentralized Online Social Networks: An Overview of Technical and Societal Challenges in Architectural Choices
note: Survey of the architectures of Mastodon, Bluesky, Hive and Nostr, including how posts propagate.

title: Kerblam: Anonymous Messaging System Protecting Both Senders and Recipients
bitmessage_link: Combines sender mixing with oblivious message retrieval for the recipient, directly targeting Bitmessage's two privacy goals.
note: Cost model: two non-colluding servers; combines the HomeRun oblivious-message-retrieval protocol with an oblivious shuffle, then extends to larger messages with a two-server distributed scheme. Receivers need not stay online or trust an online proxy; no cap on messages sent or received. Trust: two non-colluding servers. See paper for throughput.

title: Leveraging FPGAs for Homomorphic Matrix-Vector Multiplication in Oblivious Message Retrieval
bitmessage_link: Removes the need for every recipient to download and trial-decrypt the whole board, which is Bitmessage's recipient-ambiguity mechanism, while keeping the server blind to who each message is for; stronger than a fuzzy filter but needs FHE o
note: FPGA accelerator for the homomorphic matrix-vector multiplication that dominates OMR detection (high-level synthesis, design-space exploration); 13.86x speedup over the software implementation. Hardware route to lowering the server cost per scanned message.

title: Metadata-private Messaging without Coordination (PingPong)
bitmessage_link: Removes the need for sender and receiver to agree on a rendezvous address in advance, like Bitmessage's shared object pool but with enclave-protected retrieval.
note: Cost model: prototype with 32 8-core servers with enclaves; evaluated on a real messaging metadata dataset. Trust: trusted execution environments plus non-colluding servers (TEE trust).

title: RHQC: post-quantum ratcheted key exchange from coding assumptions
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Turns the HQC code-based cryptosystem into a ratcheted key exchange, giving a first code-based RKE with perfect forward secrecy and post-compromise security as a non-lattice alternative to ML-KEM ratchets.

title: Comprehensive Deniability Analysis of Signal Handshake Protocols: X3DH, PQXDH to Fully Post-Quantum with Deniable Ring Signatures
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Unified deniability framework for Signal handshake protocols; shows X3DH deniability holds under a clean AKE definition, finds PQXDH's classical authentication weakens it, and builds a fully post-quantum handshake with deniable ring signatures; compares all prior notions.

title: Myco: Unlocking Polylogarithmic Accesses in Metadata-Private Messaging
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's download-everything-and-trial-decrypt receiver privacy with PIR mailboxes, so the recipient fetches one slot without revealing which.
note: Cost model: oblivious data structure instead of PIR, so server work is O(N log^2 N) in the number of users N versus quadratic O(N^2) for PIR systems; throughput up to 302x better than multi-server and 2,219x better than single-server PIR-based systems. Trust: asymmetric two-server distributed trust (clients write to one server that obliviously forwards to a second server clients read from).

title: Automotive Middleware Performance: Comparison of FastDDS, Zenoh and vSomeIP
note: This paper examines FastDDS, a widely used open-source middleware, the newly developed Zenoh middleware, and vSomeIP, COVESAs open-source implementation of SOME/IP to identify the best performing middleware for specific operating conditions.

title: Monero's Decentralized P2P Exchanges: Functionality, Adoption, and Privacy Risks
bitmessage_link: Describes Particl SMSG, a Bitmessage-inspired flooding mixnet with 48-hour retention, as the order-book transport of BasicSwap and discusses its privacy risks.
note: Evidence for a live Bitmessage derivative (SMSG). Authors read from the arXiv PDF title page.

title: A Formalization of the Correctness of the Floodsub Protocol
note: Machine-checked correctness proof of libp2p Floodsub (delivery to all subscribers) in ACL2s.

title: Security and Efficiency of Secure Group Messaging Protocols
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Thesis on CGKA/MLS: quarantined handling of inactive members (Quarantined-TreeKEM), tree-shaping to lower communication cost (Bonsai), security-efficiency trade-offs of PCS for groups.

title: DPS-IIoT: non-interactive zero-knowledge poof-inspired access control towards information-centric industrial internet of things
note: Zero-knowledge-proof-inspired non-interactive access control for information-centric pub/sub in industrial IoT.

title: InstantOMR: Oblivious Message Retrieval with Low Latency and Optimal Parallelizability
bitmessage_link: Removes the need for every recipient to download and trial-decrypt the whole board, which is Bitmessage's recipient-ambiguity mechanism, while keeping the server blind to who each message is for; stronger than a fuzzy filter but needs FHE o
note: Hybrid of TFHE functional bootstrapping and RLWE operations; messages are processed independently so the detector can stream and answer the moment the recipient comes online. About 860x lower latency than SophOMR and near-optimal scaling with cores.

title: Lattice-based Multi-message Multi-recipient KEM/PKE with Malicious Security
bitmessage_link: Cuts the per-recipient ciphertext cost of sending one message to many addresses, relevant to chans and group delivery over a shared board.
note: Attacks existing lattice multi-recipient PKE with maliciously crafted keys (breaks semantic and key privacy) and gives the first lattice mmKEM safe against them; ciphertext for 100 recipients about 8x smaller than naive Kyber. Also improves batched random OT and group OMR.

title: Phantom Events: Demystifying the Issues of Log Forgery in Blockchain
note: Studies forged smart-contract event logs, which off-chain subscribers rely on.

title: Mix DoS Protection
bitmessage_link: Admission control for mix traffic, the mixnet equivalent of Bitmessage proof of work.
note: Design for protecting mix nodes from flooding by senders: per-packet proofs and rate limits at the first hop. Adversary: spammer or Sybil sender that floods mix nodes with packets.

title: RLN DoS Protection for Mixnet
bitmessage_link: Zero-knowledge rate limit as mixnet admission.
note: Mix DoS protection using RLN proofs per Sphinx packet. Adversary: sender exceeding its per-epoch message allowance or replaying proofs across mix nodes.

title: Multi-message_id Burn RLN
bitmessage_link: Burst budget for rate limiting.
note: RLN variant where a user can burn several message ids in one proof to send a burst. Adversary: spammer reusing message ids.

title: InsPIRe: Communication-Efficient PIR with Server-side Preprocessing
bitmessage_link: Replaces broadcast-and-trial-decrypt with indexed private retrieval: the recipient fetches only its slots and the server learns nothing about which; works only if the recipient can compute or look up the slot (a rendezvous or mailbox index)
note: High throughput and low query size with only server-side preprocessing (no offline download): versus YPIR, 5x smaller keys, up to 50% less online query communication and up to 25% higher throughput.

title: LLMix: Quantifying Mix Network Privacy Erosion with Generative Models
bitmessage_link: Learning-based adversary measuring how repeated observations erode mixnet anonymity over time (long-term intersection, which Bitmessage chans suffer too).
note: Cost model: no system cost; shows a clear relation between number of captured messages and privacy loss, and that equal average-latency strategies are not equally unlinkable.

title: Post-Quantum Stealth Address Protocols
bitmessage_link: Stealth addressing has the same recipient-scan cost structure as Bitmessage's trial decryption; post-quantum version quantifies it.
note: Three lattice stealth address protocols (LWE, Ring-LWE, Module-LWE); Module-LWE (Kyber-style) SAP scans the ephemeral public key registry about 66.8% faster than the elliptic-curve pairing SAP. Recipient detection is scan-and-test, so ciphertext size sets scanning bandwidth.

title: MSC4268: Sharing room keys for past messages
bitmessage_link: Joiner-gets-history is the normal case in Bitmessage chans (anyone with the passphrase reads everything); Matrix makes it an explicit policy.
note: Lets new room members receive keys for earlier messages. Weakens forward-secrecy in exchange for usability; metadata is unchanged.

title: MSC4297: State Resolution v2.1
bitmessage_link: none direct (federated access control)
note: Modifies state resolution to reduce 'state resets' (access-control failures in a decentralised event DAG), room version 11 base.

title: OPTIMUMP2P: Fast and Reliable Gossiping in P2P Networks
note: RLNC-based gossip (Optimum P2P / mump2p) compared with GossipSub in a 36-node geo-distributed A/B test.

title: OPTIMUMP2P Demo: Fast and Reliable Gossiping in P2P Networks
note: Demo paper accompanying OptimumP2P.

title: Practical Deniable Post-Quantum X3DH: A Lightweight Split-KEM for K-Waay
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Sparrow-KEM and Sym-Sparrow-KEM: lightweight split KEMs that shrink K-Waay (post-quantum deniable X3DH) to sizes competitive with ring-signature designs, with a 40x speedup; Sym-Sparrow-KEM is the first symmetric split KEM offering deniability, IND-1KCA and IND-1BatchCCA security; keeps asynchrony and deniability.

title: NIST IR 8545: Status Report on the Fourth Round of the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization Process
bitmessage_link: HQC's multi-KB ciphertexts make it unusable per message in a flooding network; relevant only as an algorithm-diversity backup.
note: Selects HQC (code-based, quasi-cyclic syndrome decoding) as a backup KEM to ML-KEM, with a draft standard planned; BIKE and Classic McEliece not selected. Table 7 (bytes) for HQC-128/192/256: encapsulation key 2249/4522/7245, decapsulation key 40, ciphertext 4497/9042/14485; BIKE level 1/3/5 for comparison: key 1541/3083/5122, ciphertext 1573/3115/5154. The 2025 HQC specification later changes these to 2241/4514/7237

title: Paprika: Replica Placement for Multi-Region Edge Publish-Subscribe Systems
note: Abstract not retrieved; classified from the title as core work on IoT/edge.

title: PANDAS: Peer-to-peer, Adaptive Networking for Data Availability Sampling within Ethereum Consensus Timebounds
note: Direct-dissemination p2p design for data availability sampling, contrasted with GossipSub subnets and DHT approaches.

title: Whom do you trust? PRISM: Lightweight Key Transparency for All
bitmessage_link: Blockchain-style public append-only directory as the trust anchor, a direction relevant to chain-anchored messengers.
note: PRISM: lightweight key transparency with a zero-knowledge virtual machine 'rollup' on a third-party data availability layer so every user automatically checks the whole directory's integrity; claims large performance gains over custom ZK circuits.

title: LAMP: Lightweight Approaches for Latency Minimization in Mixnets with Practical Deployment Considerations
bitmessage_link: Practical latency reduction evaluated on latency data from the deployed Nym mixnet.
note: Cost model: 7.5x latency cut (153.4 ms to 20 ms) while keeping high anonymity; 3x better latency-anonymity trade-off than LARMix at about 13,900x lower compute.

title: MALARIA: Management of Low-Latency Routing Impact on Mix Network Anonymity
bitmessage_link: Quantifies how low-latency routing changes anonymity so that operators can choose a safe point.
note: Cost model: analysis of anonymity cost of latency-aware routing; no system numbers.

title: MOCHA: Mixnet Optimization Considering Honest Client Anonymity
bitmessage_link: Optimises mixnet routing for the anonymity of honest clients.
note: Cost model: routing optimisation; see paper for latency/anonymity numbers.

title: RFC 9794: Terminology for Post-Quantum Traditional Hybrid Schemes
bitmessage_link: Common terms for the hybrid wrappers a successor would put around every key exchange.
note: Defines vocabulary (PQ/T hybrid key encapsulation, hybrid signature, composite versus non-composite) so hybrid designs can be compared; no sizes. Reference for the hybrid KEM and hybrid signature terms used across this slice.

title: Session Protocol V2: PFS, Post-Quantum and the Future of Private Messaging
bitmessage_link: Concrete statement that static long-term-key encryption (as in Bitmessage) lacks forward secrecy, and that ratchets are hard in decentralised multi-device storage.
note: Proposed V2: per-device and per-account rotating keys for forward secrecy, ML-KEM post-quantum KEM, authorised device management. States V1 weaknesses: single long-term key, no forward secrecy after Signal protocol was dropped, harvest-now-decrypt-later, nodes that retain messages past the 14-day TTL. Content and session properties only; routing metadata unchanged.

title: Eclipse Attacks on Monero's Peer-to-Peer Network
bitmessage_link: An eclipsed node loses Dandelion-style source hiding and sees only attacker traffic; peer-selection hardening is a prerequisite for stem-phase privacy.
note: First practical eclipse of Monero: classic eclipse attacks fail against its connection manager, so the attacker forces the target to reset benign connections and reconnect to malicious nodes (no restart needed); countermeasures reported to the Monero team. Adversary: remote attacker with several malicious nodes that exploits connection-management rules; relevant because Dandelion++ privacy relies on honest outbound p

title: zk-promises: Anonymous Moderation, Reputation, and Blocking from Anonymous Credentials with Callbacks
bitmessage_link: Anonymous reputation and revocation, the missing counterpart to Bitmessage's unaccountable senders.
note: Anonymous credentials with callbacks: a server can later ban, penalise or update reputation of an anonymous user without learning who they are. Adversary: misbehaving anonymous user who tries to evade moderation, and server trying to link sessions.

title: The ML-KEM Braid Protocol
bitmessage_link: Shows the bandwidth cost of continuous PQ key agreement, directly relevant to constraints in flood-style networks.
note: Sparse continuous key agreement using incremental ML-KEM, adding PQ post-compromise security to the Signal ratchet (triple ratchet). Content/session security only.

title: Privacy-Preserving Authentication: Theory vs. Practice
bitmessage_link: Orientation on rate-limiting and anonymous-admission primitives.
note: Survey of anonymous credentials, group/ring signatures and deployed systems, including the state of post-quantum constructions and why none is yet competitive with classical sizes.

title: TEEMS: A Trusted Execution Environment based Metadata-protected Messaging System
bitmessage_link: Enclave-based oblivious mailbox: servers hold messages in TEEs and route obliviously, so no flooding or trial decryption is needed.
note: Cost model: 220 clients in conversations in under 1 s with 205 cores, 18x better latency and throughput than prior work. Trust: TEE integrity and confidentiality (side channels excluded or mitigated by oblivious algorithms); distributed enclaves.

title: Generic Anonymity Wrapper for Messaging Protocols
bitmessage_link: Gives a way to put receiver anonymity with forward and post-compromise guarantees on top of a ratcheting session, where Bitmessage uses static address keys.
note: Anonymity Wrapper primitive that wraps ciphertexts of an existing messaging protocol (e.g. Signal) so they look random, with forward anonymity and post-compromise anonymity under state exposure; sender and receiver update algorithms refresh the anonymity state.

title: Amortized PQ MLS Combiner (draft-ietf-mls-combiner-02)
bitmessage_link: Shows how to pay the post-quantum bandwidth cost only occasionally in a group session.
note: Combines a traditional MLS session with a post-quantum MLS session by seeding the exporter secret of the PQ session into the traditional one; supports cheap traditional-only (PARTIAL) and hybrid PQ (FULL) key updates so that PQ KEM and signature cost is amortised while keeping frequent key rotation; targets amortised PQ confidentiality and authenticity.

title: Cloud-edge MQTT messaging for latency mitigation and broker memory footprint reduction
note: Empirical and analytical validations have demonstrated the performance of the proposed design in latency mitigation, and the result shows that, empirically, the proposed design may save the run-time broker memory footprint by about 75%.

title: EFPIX: An Encrypted Flood Protocol for Metadata-Resistant Communication
bitmessage_link: A modern flood-relay design in Bitmessage style: PoW, dedup and aging against spam, per-correspondent aliases so recipients do not trial-decrypt everything.
note: Single-author preprint; cites Bitmessage for identity management and compares features in a table.

title: DANDELION (Waku v2 Dandelion)
bitmessage_link: Stem-and-fluff propagation for Waku relay to hide the originating node; the source-anonymity technique Bitmessage never used.
note: Living spec; year approximate; sibling slices hold copies (2025-waku-dandelion-spec).

title: DANDELION (Logos/Waku application specification)
bitmessage_link: Applies Dandelion to a gossip publish/subscribe messenger, the closest modern analogue of Bitmessage-style flooding plus a source-hiding stem.
note: Raw-status specification of a Dandelion-style stem/fluff layer for Waku relay messages. Adversary: passive observers among relay peers who attribute a message to the first peer to deliver it.

title: WAKU-MIX
bitmessage_link: A mixnet layer in front of a gossip pub/sub, the post-Bitmessage design point for sender anonymity.
note: Libp2p-based mixnet integration for Waku (sphinx packets, per-hop delays) giving sender anonymity for publish and request-response. Adversary: global passive observer limited by delay mixing, with some malicious mix nodes.

title: A Verification Framework for Secure Group Messaging
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Thesis covering the verified specification and implementation of MLS components (TreeSync authenticated group state, TreeKEM symbolic analysis, DY* framework); summarises the properties proved: group-state agreement, confidentiality, forward secrecy, PCS.

title: TreeKEM: A Modular Machine-Checked Symbolic Security Analysis of Group Key Agreement in Messaging Layer Security
bitmessage_link: Group-key assurance level that chan-style shared secrets cannot reach.
note: Machine-checked symbolic analysis of RFC 9420 TreeKEM that models the precise protocol (not an abstraction) and proves confidentiality, forward secrecy and post-compromise security with respect to bounded compromise, in a modular way (TreeSync, TreeKEM, TreeDEM).

title: Time will Tell: Large-scale De-anonymization of Hidden I2P Services via Live Behavior Alignment (Extended Version)
bitmessage_link: Recent I2P attack showing behavioural correlation defeats garlic routing.
note: I2PERCEPTION: low-cost method that reveals IP addresses of I2P hidden services by deploying floodfill routers to passively collect RouterInfo and aligning publication behaviour with live service behaviour. Adversary: attacker running floodfill routers (no need to control tunnel participants), passive.

title: Early-MFC: Enhanced Flow Correlation Attacks on Tor via Multi-view Triplet Networks with Early Network Traffic
bitmessage_link: Correlation needs only short traces, so short Tor sessions for a messenger are not safe.
note: Early-MFC: flow correlation using only the early part of a connection via multi-view triplet networks over payload sizes and inter-packet delays. Adversary: passive observer of both ends of a Tor connection who must decide quickly from short traces.

title: Ilyazh-Web3E2E: A Post-Quantum Hybrid Protocol for Forward-Secure Decentralized Messaging
bitmessage_link: Decentralised-identity messaging with post-quantum hybrid ratcheting, a Bitmessage-like setting; security arguments are informal.
note: Proposes a post-quantum hybrid messaging protocol for Web3 identities: Double Ratchet extended with hybrid KEM (X25519 plus ML-KEM), hybrid authentication (Ed25519 plus ML-DSA) and re-encapsulation ratcheting; claims forward secrecy and post-compromise security; IND-CCA and AKE arguments are only sketched, with comparisons to PQXDH and PQ3 (single-author preprint without a full proof).

title: IBE and PIR from Isogenies
bitmessage_link: A route to identity-addressed, recipient-hiding encryption (the Bitmessage address model) with post-quantum security.
note: First isogeny-based identity-based encryption (with anonymity: ciphertexts hide the recipient identity) and first isogeny-based single-server PIR with polylogarithmic communication; plausibly post-quantum. Theory result, no concrete costs.

title: AetherWeave: Sybil-Resistant Robust Peer Discovery with Stake
note: We present AetherWeave, a stake-backed peer-discovery protocol that ties network participation to deposited stake, raising the cost of large-scale attacks.

title: Private Information Retrieval: A Tutorial and Survey
bitmessage_link: Replaces broadcast-and-trial-decrypt with indexed private retrieval: the recipient fetches only its slots and the server learns nothing about which; works only if the recipient can compute or look up the slot (a rendezvous or mailbox index)
note: Tutorial and survey: information-theoretic and computational PIR, single and multi-server, with and without preprocessing, plus keyword and batch PIR; compares concrete efficiency of paradigms and gives guidance for choosing one.

title: Symmetric and Asymmetric Anonymous Authenticated KEM
bitmessage_link: Building block for sender- and recipient-anonymous encrypted objects with authentication, the missing piece in Bitmessage's static-key encryption.
note: Formal confidentiality, authenticity and anonymity notions for authenticated KEM with optional pre-shared keys, and efficient constructions for each key-combination; anonymity of senders and receivers is the focus.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates and Mitigations
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage addresses use secp256k1 keys; a quantum ECDLP solver recovers private keys from published public keys and decrypts recorded objects.
note: Resource estimates for breaking 256-bit elliptic-curve discrete logs (the secp256k1 curve underlying Bitcoin and Bitmessage's ECDSA/ECIES keys) and mitigation paths including migration to post-quantum signatures; relevant for exposure of long-lived static public keys.

title: PSMark: A Distributed IoT Benchmark for Publish/Subscribe Under Domain-Based Workloads
note: The Publish/Subscribe (pub/sub) paradigm is widely used in the Internet of Things (IoT).

title: Anonymity of X-Wing and its Variants
bitmessage_link: First anonymity proof for the default hybrid KEM, so hybrid post-quantum ciphertexts can serve as recipient-hidden objects.
note: First anonymity analysis of X-Wing (ML-KEM-768 + X25519; 1216 B public key, 1120 B ciphertext). Proves in the standard model that weak anonymity of any IND-CCA KEM implies full ANO-CCA (tight, memory-tight), then in the ROM that X-Wing is weakly anonymous if both X25519 (unconditionally) and ML-KEM-768 are; proposes a memory-tight variant and improves the original IND-CCA proof.

title: Better Security Proofs for X3DH and XHMQV
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Tight security reductions for X3DH and its enhancement XHMQV under multi-user DH assumptions, so that concrete security with Curve25519 and XEdDSA approaches the intended 128-bit level instead of losing a factor in the number of sessions.

title: Kopis: A KEM for Obfuscation
bitmessage_link: Candidate recipient-anonymous, random-looking encapsulation for hidden-recipient objects.
note: Module-LWE based KEM specified so that public keys and ciphertexts are uniform bytestrings, removing the hash-to-vector, matrix-expansion and ciphertext-decompression machinery that obfuscating protocols (PAKE, OKEX) need to bolt onto ML-KEM. Alternative to Kemeleon encodings.

title: Analysis and Attacks on the Reputation System of Nym
bitmessage_link: Attacks on the Nym reputation mechanism that decides which nodes carry traffic.
note: Cost model: none (attack analysis). Nym context stated in the paper: more than 550 nodes in 64 countries and about 3 billion packets per day; gateway plus up to three mix hops plus gateway; operators stake tokens and are selected into an active set by reputation. The paper attacks this reputation and selection system.

title: Automated formal analysis of Signal’s Double Ratchet: attacks, fixes and security proofs
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: First formal analysis of the Double Ratchet that covers all features (including out-of-order arrivals), highly automated, over all key compromises, and proves post-compromise security (PCS); partial results for header-encrypted and PQ-extended variants; reports attacks on earlier or alternative versions and fixes.

title: When Discovery Becomes a Storm: A ROS 2 Discovery Model for Wireless Robotic Networks
note: In Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2), Data Distribution Service (DDS) participants must discover one another before exchanging data.

title: Anamorphic Messaging: Analyzing the Double Ratchet, Triple Ratchet, PQ3, and MLS
bitmessage_link: Coercion-resistance angle: a hidden channel under key-surrender duress; relevant to deniability and plausible deniability threat models.
note: Shows how anamorphic (hidden double-key) messages can be embedded in the Double Ratchet, Triple Ratchet, PQ3 and MLS randomness and key material, so a user forced to surrender keys can still convey hidden messages; analyses what each ratchet design leaves as embeddable spots.

title: Privacy Coins Under Viewing Key Compromise
bitmessage_link: Delegating detection (view or detection keys) is the same trust move FMD and OMR make; this paper measures what an incoming-view-key holder learns.
note: Provable anonymity guarantees for Zcash and Firo when the incoming viewing key is compromised, problems with Monero, and ways a malicious party can surrender all view keys yet evade monitoring. Delegated detection capability has a privacy price.

title: OmniSphinx: Active Mix Networks
bitmessage_link: Packet-format level defence against active attacks on Sphinx-like mixnets.
note: Cost model: see paper (mix network design resisting active adversaries).

title: Hidden Services Protocol for Mixnets
bitmessage_link: Receiver-anonymous services inside a mixnet; the mixnet analogue of Bitmessage's recipient privacy without flooding.
note: Cost model: raising the Sphinx payload from 2 KiB to 10 KiB cuts mean page-load latency about 5.2x and payload overhead from 21.7 to 4.3 percent versus the current Nym baseline; deeper rewrap adds 0.3 to 0.6 s. Finds first/last-hop attacks on Nym SURB replies. Authorship list shows three names on the title page; further names may exist.

title: The Cost of Stability: Deanonymizing Onion Services Long-Lived Introduction Circuits
bitmessage_link: Persistent circuit state in onion services as a deanonymisation surface for long-running receivers.
note: Intersection attack that exploits onion-service introduction circuits fixed for 18-24 hours: an adaptive adversary observing one relay at a time reconstructs the full circuit and locates the service; on live Tor, nine of nine runs succeeded with median time about 2.2 hours. Adversary: adaptive observer of one Tor relay at a time (a compromised or malicious relay), no global view.

title: Are we collaborative yet? A Usability Perspective on Mixnet Latency for Real-Time Applications
bitmessage_link: User study on whether Nym-class latency suits real-time collaboration.
note: Cost model: measures mixnet latency tolerance with users; compares with Tor latency.

title: DKVE: Decentralized Key Validation for End-to-End Encrypted Messaging
bitmessage_link: Decentralised key validation addresses the key-binding problem Bitmessage avoids with self-certifying addresses, at the price of unreadable names.
note: Validates a contact's public key by cross-checking with mutual contacts in the social graph (OPRF and oblivious key-value stores to keep queries and contact lists private; sequential probability ratio test to detect server misbehaviour); simulations detect man-in-the-middle attacks above 97 percent for strong-to-moderate-tie networks; complements, does not replace, key transparency and out-of-band checks.

title: Anonymous Credit Tokens (draft-schlesinger-cfrg-act-01)
bitmessage_link: Budgeted anonymous admission (credits per request) as a generalisation of one-token-per-message stamps.
note: Anonymous credit tokens carrying a spendable balance: the client spends part of the credit per request and receives change, with unlinkable presentation and double-spend prevention. Adversary: client trying to double-spend or overspend; issuer trying to link spends.

title: Private Identity-based Bulletin Boards for Anonymous Messaging and Other Online Services
bitmessage_link: Lets a sender post to a receiver known only by an identity (email address, pseudonym) without prior key exchange; Bitmessage addresses are such identities.
note: Cost model: HIBE with searchable ciphertexts; posts to non-colluding servers and receiver retrieval later; see paper for latency and throughput. Trust: non-colluding servers.

title: Verbeth: Secure Messaging with Metadata Minimization over Public Blockchain Logs
bitmessage_link: Closest modern relative of Bitmessage: public log as the transport, first contact by KEM with trial decryption (or a TEE-backed private signaling service), then per-conversation topic rotation so conversations are unlinkable.
note: Cost model: no server of its own; economics and size limits of on-chain messaging analysed; first-contact discovery either long-term-key KEM with trial decryption (cost grows with the log) or private signaling backed by trusted hardware; topic rotation driven by the double-ratchet state. Main contribution is an analysis of metadata leakage under several adversaries.

title: Signal and Ready to MINGLE: In-Band Gossip for Key Transparency Split-View Detection in E2EE Messengers
bitmessage_link: Uses message traffic itself as the gossip channel, much as a gossip or flooding overlay would.
note: MINGLE: opportunistic in-band gossip of compact key-transparency commitments piggybacked on ordinary E2EE messages so that clients detect split-view equivocation without third-party auditors.

title: Metadata Analysis and Forensic Resilience Evaluation of Decentralized Messaging Applications Using NIST SP 800-86
bitmessage_link: Forensic recovery experiment on Session and BitChat: 47 message records recovered for Session, 12 BLE hop events for BitChat; evidence of what local metadata a flooding mesh leaves.
note: Diamond OA. Small experiment on one rooted phone.

title: UnifOMR: Oblivious Message Retrieval with Near-optimal Concrete Efficiency
bitmessage_link: Gives the receiver-privacy cost floor: a Bitmessage-style recipient-hiding retrieval is at best PIR-cost, which bounds what any non-broadcast design can save.
note: Shows OMR with strong detection-key-unlinkability is at least as hard as PIR (so OMR cannot be much cheaper than PIR), then builds UnifOMR on batch PIR as a black box. 2^19 messages of 612 bytes: about 25 s server time and 4 MB communication, versus over 1250 s and 260 KB for SophOMR (20x-1080x faster); costs are linear-size digests and two rounds.

title: BLOCKCHAIN-ENABLED PUBLISH-SUBSCRIBE ARCHITECTURE FOR SECURE IoT HEALTHCARE DATA TRANSMISSION
note: The flexibility of the Internet of Things significantly helps the rapid deployment of health data transfer.

title: Send and Pretend: Exploiting Transcript Consistency Issues in End-to-End Encrypted Group Chats
bitmessage_link: Participant/transcript consistency is a property store-and-forward flooding gives no help with; Bitmessage chans have no consistency guarantee either.
note: Shows that WhatsApp, Signal, iMessage, Threema and others guarantee no transcript consistency in group chats: a malicious member can selectively omit, reorder or alter content per recipient (via fallback paths or pairwise channels inside groups) without UI warnings, e.g. to rig polls; outlines low-overhead mitigations and UI signalling.

title: Hey there! You are using WhatsApp: Enumerating Three Billion Accounts for Security and Privacy
bitmessage_link: Phone-number identifiers make the directory enumerable; Bitmessage's key-derived addresses avoid enumeration but give up discovery.
note: Probed over a hundred million phone numbers per hour against WhatsApp contact discovery without effective rate limiting; census of the user base; nearly half of numbers from the 2021 Facebook leak still active; found reuse of X25519 keys across devices and numbers. Shows an identifier-based directory leaks registration status and metadata at planetary scale despite E2EE.

title: Oblivious Ciphertext Compression via Linear Codes
bitmessage_link: Cheaper digest step for the board-scan outsourcing that replaces Bitmessage's trial decryption.
note: Deterministic, perfectly correct oblivious compression and decompression of sparse encrypted vectors via linear codes; targets the compression step in OMR, PIR and encrypted search with smaller ciphertexts or lower compute than earlier schemes.

title: Collaborative Rate Limiting Nullifier Signaling
note: We introduce Collaborative RLN Signaling (coRLN), a protocol that lets $n$ parties register as a single RLN member and signal only by acting jointly.

title: Aegon: Self-Auditable Key Transparency
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Aegon: key transparency whose server computation depends only on the updates in the current epoch (no per-epoch global invariance proofs), enabling short epochs and auditing by lightweight end users instead of global third-party auditors.

title: SoK: Outsourced Private Set Intersection
bitmessage_link: Bitmessage avoids contact discovery by publishing everything, but any scheme that routes by address or tag must solve how a user learns the right address or slot without revealing their contacts.
note: Framework of 12 properties (security, functionality, efficiency) and analysis of 20 outsourced PSI protocols where clients delegate the heavy work to an untrusted server, with an interactive selection tool and gaps relative to ordinary PSI.

title: Secrecy in Squirrel and the Post-Compromise Security of a Ratchet
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: First mechanised computational-model proof of a ratchet's post-compromise security (using the Squirrel prover), covering a Signal-style ratchet; shows secrecy of session keys under state compromise with healing.

title: Lower Bounds for PIR with Preprocessing from Blackbox Cryptography
bitmessage_link: Rules out sublinear-cost private retrieval by black-box means, the 'no free lunch' behind trial-decrypt-everything.
note: Unconditional: if the client stores s bits about an n-bit database, then answering k = Omega(s) queries requires either Omega(n/s) amortized online communication or Omega(n/s) amortized server cryptographic operations, for schemes using any cryptography in a black-box way (random oracles, virtual black-box obfuscation). Tight against known constructions; also bounds for symmetric PIR with client preprocessing.

title: Techreport: Evaluating Tor-based Location Privacy for Ethereum Validators
note: Evaluates 'Tor push' dissemination integrated with GossipSub to mitigate validator deanonymization.

title: X3DH with Deniable Authentication without Trusted Third Parties
bitmessage_link: Decentralised, directory-free authentication in the style of Bitmessage's out-of-band address exchange.
