note: Extends X3DH to message authentication in the short-authenticated-string model (no trusted third party) using a VRF-based SAS scheme on ephemeral keys, keeping deniability and adding authentication without a PKI.

title: Forget-me-not Trees: Mass-scale Auditable Key Transparency from Hash Functions
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Forget-me-not trees (Merkle trees plus Bloom filters): key transparency with audit proofs about 500x smaller (from 15-30 MB to 30-60 KB), relying only on hash functions.

title: StreamRTPS: Increasing DDS Bandwidth Efficiency by Reducing Protocol Overhead
note: In this paper, we propose three extensions to the Real-Time Publish Subscribe wire protocol, on which Data Distribution Service (DDS) is based, to improve bandwidth efficiency.

title: Lean Gossip: Big Gains From Small Talk
note: First systematic simulation sweep of GossipSub D and D_lazy under 0-30% churn in 1000 nodes; lean configs dominate Ethereum's deployed settings. Author-hosted preprint.

title: Post-Quantum Traditional (PQ/T) Hybrid Key Agreement Mechanisms for TLS 1.3
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Standards-track hybrid key agreements for TLS 1.3 combining ECDHE (X25519, secp256r1/384r1) with ML-KEM (e.g. X25519MLKEM768); concretises the hybrid combiner with FIPS 203 KEMs; IND-CCA security if either component holds.

title: LetoPIR: Fast Keyword Private Information Retrieval with Logarithmic Communication
bitmessage_link: Lowest-communication keyword lookup so far, directly usable for topic or tag retrieval.
note: Hintless keyword PIR with logarithmic communication: 12.4x-17.0x less communication than SparsePIR (USENIX'23) for databases of 256 MB to 4 GB with 256-byte records and over 3x less computation at 256 MB; 51.4x-184.8x less communication than KPIR (USENIX'25) at similar or better computation. Notes that Apple already deploys PIR for real-time caller ID lookup.

title: Pepper: High-bandwidth and Scalable Anonymous Broadcast with Cryptographic Privacy
bitmessage_link: Replaces Bitmessage's flood-and-trial-decrypt with DC-net rounds: every client sends every round, so the recipient/sender is hidden without proof-of-work, but the anonymity set is bounded by the round size.
note: Cost model: DC-net with DPFs; millisecond-level registration audits, thousands of channels, 1.2 to 20x higher effective messaging rates than state-of-the-art alternatives (per abstract). Authorship list truncated to the first three names shown on the title page.

title: DAIS-MQTT: A Distributed MQTT Communication Method Based on Intelligent QoS Routing and Hierarchical Collaboration
note: This paper proposes a distributed MQTT communication method based on intelligent QoS routing and hierarchical collaboration (DAIS-MQTT), which effectively addresses the scalability limitation of centralized proxies by enabling multi-level proxy...

title: SECUREVENT: Hybrid AI/ML Security Monitoring for Distributed Event-Based Systems
note: This paper proposes SECUREVENT, a hybrid AI/ML security-monitoring architecture for distributed event-based systems.

title: Security analysis: Bitmessage vulnerability assessment regarding quantum computing threats (PyBitmessage issue 2344)
bitmessage_link: Argues that secp256k1 static keys plus public storage of all ciphertext make Bitmessage a harvest-now-decrypt-later target; no forward secrecy, no post-quantum KEM.
note: Short issue text by an individual maintainer of forks (MiNode-Refined, PyBitRefined); weak as a paper but dated and technical, so kept as report.

title: Aquaman: A Transparent Proxy Architecture for Quantum Resilient Key Establishment
bitmessage_link: Illustrates the record-now-decrypt-later threat model; limited technical overlap.
note: Harvest-now-decrypt-later framing; proxy offloads PQC or splits a session key across diverse media with recovery probability decaying as (B/d)^n; 1000-run EC2 prototype. Weak relevance: engineering prototype, no anonymity analysis.

title: Onion-Routed Multi-Circuit Key Establishment for Quantum-Resilient Sessions
bitmessage_link: Alternative to post-quantum primitives for long-term confidentiality; relies on the anonymity network itself.
note: Splits a session key into fragments sent over distinct ephemeral Tor circuits so an adversary must deanonymize every circuit; prototype takes 13-20 s on average (about 88% Tor delay). Argument is a correlation bound, not a post-quantum primitive.

title: Auditable Continuous Group Key Agreement
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Auditable CGKA: lets a designated auditor recover past epoch keys and verify recovery remains possible, without a silent escrow; targets regulated sectors that otherwise log plaintext.

title: Key Transparency Architecture (draft-ietf-keytrans-architecture-09)
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Terminology, interaction patterns and security properties of Key Transparency in group-messaging deployments; specifies what the protocol guarantees (and what it cannot, e.g. split-view defence needs gossip or third-party auditors).

title: Key Transparency Protocol (draft-ietf-keytrans-protocol-05)
bitmessage_link: Directory-based answer to the binding of names to keys that Bitmessage sidesteps with self-certifying addresses.
note: Protocol for a third-party-auditable key directory: a prefix tree of versioned keys inside a log; clients get inclusion/non-inclusion proofs, monotonicity and consistency checks; claims users either get the true key bindings or detect interference.

title: Optimum Peer-Turbo: A Scalable and Efficient Solution for P2P Broadcasting
note: Coded broadcast for tree/star shard propagation under bounded time windows (Solana/Monad style).

title: Byzantine-resilient peer sampling for large-scale distributed systems
note: Thesis on Byzantine-tolerant peer sampling, a membership building block for gossip dissemination.

title: Security Analysis of Bitcoin's V2 Transport Protocol: Exploiting Design Implications for Sustained Eclipse and Downgrade Attacks
bitmessage_link: Encrypted transport alone does not remove length leakage or downgrade risk for a flooding network; relevant to any messenger that layers transport encryption under flooding.
note: Security analysis of Bitcoin V2 (BIP324) encrypted P2P transport: a network-level attacker can identify application messages from TCP payload lengths, eclipse a node via properties of encrypted channels, and downgrade all connections to the unencrypted protocol using the compatibility mechanisms; validated with measurements, emulation and simulation. Adversary: on-path network-level attacker (active for eclipse and d

title: Benchmarking Message Brokers for IoT Edge Computing: A Comprehensive Performance Study
note: Asynchronous messaging is a cornerstone of modern distributed systems, enabling decoupled communication for scalable and resilient applications.

title: Silent Payments, Formally: Security, Scanning Costs, and Blind Collaborative Payments
bitmessage_link: Shows a receiver-side scan DoS: whoever can post chain data chooses the receiver's work, the same problem as Bitmessage's flood, bounded there by proof-of-work.
note: Game-based unlinkability proofs for BIP-352 and an attack-oriented analysis of receiver scan work: sender-chosen chain data lets an attacker inflate scan cost (quadratic in outputs; the 2026 Kmax cap makes it linear); any compliant scanner needs Omega(N+KM) operations; a set-probing scanner (Specs) is 39x faster on the worst case.

title: OptiMix: Scalable and Distributed Approaches for Latency Optimization in Modern Mixnets
bitmessage_link: Distributed latency optimisation for modern mixnets.
note: Cost model: distributed latency-optimisation approaches; see paper.

title: Sensing Censorship and Censuring Censors with Censorship-Evident Publishing Systems
note: We study the complementary, rarely explored goal of making any censorship attempt transparent.

title: Remise: Authorized Anonymous Communication Systems
bitmessage_link: Adds authorised-sender access control to DPF-based anonymous mailboxes; analogue of Bitmessage's PoW admission control but with credentials.
note: Cost model: two-server authorised anonymous communication on Distributed ORAM, in two modes (public anonymous bulletin board per epoch, and secret-shared channels with grantable and revocable read access); 80x lower online server time than PACL (Spectrum) for databases of size 2^24. Trust: at least one of two servers honest.

title: RFC 10024: Post-Quantum Traditional (PQ/T) Hybrid Key Agreement Mechanisms for TLS 1.3
bitmessage_link: The deployed default hybrid; fixes the wire sizes any hybrid design is compared with.
note: Standardises X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768 and SecP384r1MLKEM1024. X25519MLKEM768 client share is 1216 bytes (1184 ML-KEM encapsulation key + 32 X25519) and server share 1120 bytes (1088 ML-KEM ciphertext + 32); secp256r1 variant client share carries a 65-byte point plus the 1184-byte ML-KEM key.

title: From Specs to Apps: Verifying and Monitoring Models of Signal and WhatsApp
bitmessage_link: none direct
note: Applies the SpecMon runtime monitor to WhatsApp Web and Signal Desktop to check whether observed executions conform to formal protocol models, bridging the gap between proven specifications and implementation behaviour.

title: FoSAM: Forward Secret Messaging in Ad-Hoc Networks
bitmessage_link: Forward-secret messaging for ad-hoc and mesh networks without servers; targets the missing key-evolution of flood-based messengers.
note: Preprint.

title: Rate-Limiting Nullifiers for Gasless Sequencer Admission in Ethereum Layer-2 Rollups
note: We present an idealized protocol architecture for gasless sequencer admission in Ethereum Layer-2 rollups based on Rate-Limiting Nullifiers (RLN) and a non-transferable reputation token (Karma).

title: TrustMix: How to Mix Messages in a Mobile Ad-Hoc Network
note: In this paper, we present TrustMix, a mix protocol for MANETs that operates without any central trusted party.

title: Eclipse Attacks on Ethereum's Peer-to-Peer Network
bitmessage_link: Up-to-date check that overlay-eclipse remains practical, relevant for a modern flooding messenger.
note: End-to-end eclipse of post-Merge Ethereum execution-layer nodes on restart: poisoning the discovery table, poisoning the DNS-based peer list via the official DNS crawler (28 IP addresses over 100 days) and hijacking idle incoming connection slots (outgoing redirection success from 45 to 95 percent). Adversary: remote attacker with a small set of IP addresses and patience, no network position.

title: Deanonymizing Monero Transactions in Tor Network
bitmessage_link: Anonymity-network transport plus Dandelion++ still leaks when peer selection is restricted; shows peer-selection hardening matters for source privacy.
note: ProxyMark: a Monero node using Tor sends originated transactions only to two outgoing Tor hidden-service proxy nodes before clearnet spread, so an adversary occupying those outgoing connections sees origin. Adversary: active node that fills the victim outgoing slots on the Tor path; tested on live Tor, mainnet and testnet.

title: Oblivious Signaling
bitmessage_link: Targets the same trade-off as Bitmessage's flood-and-scan model: delivering without per-recipient inboxes (which leak routing) and without every recipient scanning.
note: Asks whether a single untrusted server can support asynchronous delivery without learning destinations and without paying FHE scan cost on every retrieval. Argues OMR makes the retrieval of the whole board the central operation and pays heavy homomorphic work each time; proposes oblivious signaling as a cheaper structure. See the paper for the new construction and costs.

title: SimpleX Channels: overview and design
bitmessage_link: Publish/subscribe to a named feed without every node ingesting everything (contrast Bitmessage broadcasts).
note: Design rationale for decentralised channels: owner-signed content, redundant relays, subscriber privacy. Hides subscriber identity from relays and other subscribers; owner is known.

title: SimpleX Channels Protocol
bitmessage_link: Channels are the closest SimpleX analogue to Bitmessage chans/broadcast, with relay trust instead of flooding.
note: Protocol for one-to-many channels via chat relays, so subscribers and owners stay unlinked from relay operators' view; roles for owners, relays and subscribers.

title: DumboMix: Robust Asynchronous Anonymous Broadcast Made Practical
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.
note: Cost model: anonymous broadcast that keeps working under asynchrony; see paper for batch sizes. Trust: Byzantine fault tolerant server set.

title: Formal Security Analysis of the Olvid Messenger
bitmessage_link: A deployed messenger built with identifier-free onboarding and its own AKE/CKA, analysed against the Signal benchmark.
note: First formal (Tamarin) analysis of Olvid, an E2EE messenger without phone numbers used by French officials: verifies mutual authentication, session-key secrecy, forward secrecy and replay protection against an active adversary, but shows Olvid is not secure in the eCK model (does not meet properties of Signal-class protocols), uncovers a potential timing leakage and discusses Olvid's anonymity claims. title: Evaluating GossipSub for Data Availability Sampling Under Ethereum Consensus Deadlines
note: Master's thesis evaluating GossipSub for DAS dissemination within slot deadlines.

title: A Spatially-Aware Publish-Subscribe Middleware for IoT Applications
note: Spatial and proximity awareness are critical enablers for efficient communication in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and the Internet of Things (IoT).

title: Practical Attacks on a Decentralized Secure Messenger Session
bitmessage_link: Shows that dropping Signal's ratchet for a stateless long-term-key design reintroduces the authentication gaps of Bitmessage-style static-key schemes.
note: Implementation-driven analysis of Session Protocol V1 (1:1 and closed groups): no mutual public-key authentication and no binding to monotonic counters. Three practical attacks by malicious server nodes or insiders: impersonation via public-key substitution, message timestamp forgery, and message dropping/replay. Concerns authentication and ordering; routing metadata properties not the focus.

title: Duet: Co-Optimizing P2P Message Propagation and Rotating-Leader Consensus
note: Tree-based reliable broadcast with gossip fallback integrated into Tendermint and libp2p; up to 7.26x throughput over gossip.

title: Verifiable SelfMix
bitmessage_link: Verifiable mixing where users shuffle themselves.
note: Cost model: verifiable self-mix (VSM) for messages on a public bulletin board; users write their ciphertext to a hidden unique slot in a public table (Unique Number Selection plus Secure Mapping of Private Permutation), giving unconditional individual verifiability without trusting a mix server. Proofs in the malicious model; positioned between centralised mixnets and DC-net/MPC shuffles.

title: Deanonymizing Bitcoin Transactions via Network Traffic Analysis with Semi-supervised Learning
bitmessage_link: Machine-learning traffic analysis on top of flooding: shows source timing leakage persists under transport encryption.
note: NTSSL: transaction deanonymisation combining network traffic analysis with semi-supervised learning (pseudo-labels from unsupervised clustering) and NTSSL+ with cross-layer transaction clustering; reported 1.6x better than a prior ML approach. Adversary: passive network observer with traffic traces and few labels.

title: NIP-01: Basic protocol flow description
bitmessage_link: Events signed with the author key, relays that store and serve them by filter; defines the relay model every DM scheme runs on (relay sees pubkeys, tags and filters).
note: Living spec; year approximate (project start 2019-2020).

title: NIP-04: Encrypted Direct Message (deprecated)
bitmessage_link: Legacy DM: kind-4 event, ECDH shared secret with AES-256-CBC, sender and recipient pubkeys and timing visible to relays. Unlike Bitmessage it hides nothing about the pair.
note: Marked unrecommended in favour of NIP-17; year approximate. Practical attacks in Kimura et al. 2025.

title: NIP-13: Proof of Work
bitmessage_link: Hashcash-style leading-zero-bits proof carried in an event nonce tag; relays may require it as an anti-spam admission, the Bitmessage mechanism in a relay setting.
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: NIP-17: Private Direct Messages
bitmessage_link: Current DM scheme: NIP-44 encryption inside NIP-59 gift wraps, delivered to the relays listed in the recipient relay list; relay learns the recipient but not the sender. Receiver privacy is via relay choice, not ambiguity.
note: Living spec; year approximate (merged around 2024).

title: NIP-44: Encrypted Payloads (versioned)
bitmessage_link: ECDH + HKDF + ChaCha20 + HMAC with padding; fixes the malleability and length leak of NIP-04; still no forward secrecy.
note: Audited by Cure53 per the spec text; year approximate.

title: NIP-59: Gift Wrap
bitmessage_link: Rumor, seal, gift wrap: the author event is sealed to the recipient, then wrapped under a throw-away key with randomised timestamps; hides the sender from relays but the recipient pubkey tag stays visible unless the recipient authenticates
note: Living spec; year approximate.

title: Group Chat Specification (Katzenpost)
bitmessage_link: Group messaging on Pigeonhole boxes, the mixnet counterpart of Bitmessage chans.
note: Cost model: depends on Pigeonhole; no numbers. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).

title: KEM Sphinx Packet Format (Katzenpost specification)
bitmessage_link: KEM-based Sphinx preserving bitwise unlinkability, constant packet size and route-length hiding.
note: Cost model: replaces NIKE with KEM at the price of larger headers. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).

title: Propagation of mix decoy loop statistics (Katzenpost specification)
bitmessage_link: Defence against (n-1) attacks that use strategic packet loss: nodes publish decoy-loop statistics.
note: Cost model: extra statistics traffic with directory authority. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).

title: Katzenpost Mix Network Specification
bitmessage_link: Mix-based answer to Bitmessage's source-timing and flooding weaknesses: layered encryption and cover traffic instead of broadcasting every object to every node.
note: Cost model: high-level architecture of a Loopix-style decryption mixnet with entry, middle and service layers, directory authorities, Poisson mix delays and loop decoys; no throughput figures. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).

title: Sphinx Packet Replay Detection (Katzenpost specification)
bitmessage_link: Replay detection that Bitmessage handles with object-hash dedup; here per-hop tag caches with epoch rotation.
note: Cost model: memory per node grows with packets per epoch. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).

title: Pigeonhole Protocol Specification (Katzenpost)
bitmessage_link: Replaces mailbox servers with scattered storage: clients write and read pseudorandom boxes through the mixnet, a direct successor to Bitmessage's shared object store.
note: Cost model: box-based streams (BACAP), all-or-nothing group writes; no throughput numbers. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).

title: Katzenpost Sphinx Cryptographic Packet Format Specification
bitmessage_link: Concrete Sphinx parameterisation used by Katzenpost; the packet format layer that stops per-hop linking.
note: Cost model: fixed-size packets, per-hop DH blinding, SURB replies. Katzenpost spec (undated PDF; year is an estimate from the Echomix and Katzenpost repository history).
